translations.literal: Biographies 284: Filial Piety and Righteousness 1
translations.idiomatic: Biography 284: Filial Piety and Righteousness, Part 1

sentences.zh: 朱用純吳蕃昌從弟謙牧沈磊周靖耿燿弟炳兄子於彝

translations.literal: Zhu Yongchun, Wu Fanchang, his younger cousin Qian Mu, Shen Lei, Zhou Jing, Geng Yao, his younger brother Bing, and his elder brother's son Yu Yi
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yongchun, Wu Fanchang, Qian Mu (Fanchang's younger cousin), Shen Lei, Zhou Jing, Geng Yao, Geng Bing (Yao's younger brother), and Yu Yi (son of Yao's elder brother)

sentences.zh: 耿輔李景濂汪灝弟晨日昂日昇黃農曹亨黃嘉章

translations.literal: Geng Fu, Li Jinglian, Wang Hao, his younger brothers Chen, Ri'ang, and Risheng, Huang Nong, Cao Heng, and Huang Jiazhang
translations.idiomatic: Geng Fu, Li Jinglian, Wang Hao, Wang Chen, Ri'ang, and Risheng (Hao's younger brothers), Huang Nong, Cao Heng, and Huang Jiazhang

sentences.zh: 鄭明允劉宗洙弟恩廣恩廣子青藜何復漢許季覺

translations.literal: Zheng Mingyun, Liu Zongzhu, his younger brother Enguang, Enguang's son Qingli, He Fuhan, and Xu Jijue
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mingyun, Liu Zongzhu, Enguang (Zongzhu's younger brother), Qingli (Enguang's son), He Fuhan, and Xu Jijue

sentences.zh: 吳氏四孝子雷顯宗趙清榮漣薛文弟化禮

translations.literal: The four filial sons of the Wu family, Lei Xianzong, Zhao Qing, Rong Lian, Xue Wen, and his younger brother Huali
translations.idiomatic: The four filial sons of the Wu clan, Lei Xianzong, Zhao Qing, Rong Lian, Xue Wen, and Huali (Wen's younger brother)

sentences.zh: 曹孝童丁履豫鍾保覺羅色爾岱翁杜佟良克什布

translations.literal: Cao Xiaotong, Ding Lüyu, Zhong Bao, Jueluo Se'erdai, Weng Du, and Tongliang Keshibu
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiaotong, Ding Lüyu, Zhong Bao, Jueluo Se'erdai, Weng Du, and Tongliang Keshibu

sentences.zh: 王麟瑞李盛山李悃奚緝營周士晉黃有則

translations.literal: Wang Linrui, Li Shengshan, Li Kun, Xi Jiying, Zhou Shijin, and Huang Youze
translations.idiomatic: Wang Linrui, Li Shengshan, Li Kun, Xi Jiying, Zhou Shijin, and Huang Youze

sentences.zh: 王尚毅胡锳李三張夢維樂太希董盛祖

translations.literal: Wang Shangyi, Hu Ying, Li San, Zhang Mengwei, Yue Taixi, and Dong Shengzu
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shangyi, Hu Ying, Li San, Zhang Mengwei, Yue Taixi, and Dong Shengzu

sentences.zh: 徐守仁李鳳翔卯觀成葛大賓呂斅孚

translations.literal: Xu Shouren, Li Fengxiang, Mao Guancheng, Ge Dabin, and Lü Xuefu
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shouren, Li Fengxiang, Mao Guancheng, Ge Dabin, and Lü Xuefu

sentences.zh: 王子明馮星明張元翰俞鴻慶姜瑢湯淵魏興

translations.literal: Wang Ziming, Feng Xingming, Zhang Yuanhan, Yu Hongqing, Jiang Rong, Tang Yuan, and Wei Xing
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziming, Feng Xingming, Zhang Yuanhan, Yu Hongqing, Jiang Rong, Tang Yuan, and Wei Xing

sentences.zh: 戴兆笨潘周岱張淮張廷標胡其愛方其明鄧成珠

translations.literal: Dai Zhaoben, Pan Zhoudai, Zhang Huai, Zhang Tingbiao, Hu Qiai, Fang Qiming, and Deng Chengzhu
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhaoben, Pan Zhoudai, Zhang Huai, Zhang Tingbiao, Hu Qiai, Fang Qiming, and Deng Chengzhu

sentences.zh: 張三愛楊夢益閻天倫夏士友白長久郭味兒聶宏

translations.literal: Zhang San'ai, Yang Mengyi, Yan Tianlun, Xia Shiyou, Bai Changjiu, Guo Wei'er, and Nie Hong
translations.idiomatic: Zhang San'ai, Yang Mengyi, Yan Tianlun, Xia Shiyou, Bai Changjiu, Guo Wei'er, and Nie Hong

sentences.zh: 董阿虎張乞人席慕孔張長松崔長生榮孝子

translations.literal: Dong Ahu, Zhang Qiren, Xi Mukong, Zhang Changsong, Cui Changsheng, and Rong the filial son
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ahu, Zhang Qiren, Xi Mukong, Zhang Changsong, Cui Changsheng, and Rong the filial son

sentences.zh: 無錫二孝子啞孝子清興關外，俗純樸，愛親敬長，內愨而外嚴。

translations.literal: The two filial sons of Wuxi, the mute filial son, and the Qing rise beyond the Pass: customs were pure and plain, loving parents and respecting elders, inwardly reserved yet outwardly stern.
translations.idiomatic: Among them are the two filial sons of Wuxi, the mute filial son, and others. Since the Qing arose beyond the Pass, the people have been plain and unadorned in custom, devoted to parents and respectful to elders, reserved within yet stern without.

sentences.zh: 既定鼎，禮教益備。

translations.literal: Once the tripod was fixed, ritual instruction grew ever more complete.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynasty was firmly established, ritual instruction became ever more complete.

sentences.zh: 定旌格，循明舊。

translations.literal: Standards for commendation were fixed, following Ming precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Standards for imperial commendation were set, following the old Ming practice.

sentences.zh: 親存，奉侍竭其力；

translations.literal: While parents lived, one served them with utmost strength;
translations.idiomatic: While parents were alive, one served them with all one's strength;

sentences.zh: 親歿，善居喪，或廬於墓；

translations.literal: when parents died, one observed mourning well, sometimes dwelling in a hut by the tomb;
translations.idiomatic: when they died, one observed mourning properly, sometimes dwelling in a hut beside the grave;

sentences.zh: 親遠行，萬里行求，或生還，或以喪歸。

translations.literal: when parents traveled afar, one went ten thousand li in search, sometimes bringing them back alive, sometimes returning with their coffin.
translations.idiomatic: when parents traveled far away, one journeyed thousands of miles in search, sometimes bringing them home alive, sometimes returning with their remains.

sentences.zh: 友於兄弟，同居三五世以上，號義門，及諸義行，皆禮旌。

translations.literal: Brotherly harmony, dwelling together for three to five generations or more, called "gates of righteousness," and all such righteous conduct were honored by ritual commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Harmony among brothers, households living together for three to five generations or more and styled "gates of righteousness," and all such acts of righteousness were rewarded with ritual commendation.

sentences.zh: 親病，刲股刳肝；

translations.literal: When parents fell ill, one cut flesh from the thigh or excised the liver;
translations.idiomatic: When parents fell ill, one cut flesh from one's thigh or excised one's liver;

sentences.zh: 親喪，以身殉：皆以傷生有禁，有司以事聞，輒破格報可。

translations.literal: when parents died, one gave one's life in mourning: though harming the body was forbidden, when officials reported such cases, exceptional approval was invariably granted.
translations.idiomatic: when parents died, one gave one's own life in mourning. Although self-injury was prohibited by law, whenever officials reported such cases, exceptional approval was invariably granted.

sentences.zh: 所以教民者，若是其周其密也。

translations.literal: Thus in teaching the people, the measures were so thorough and so strict.
translations.idiomatic: In instructing the people, the measures were as thorough and as strict as this.

sentences.zh: 國史承前例，撰次孝友傳，亦頗及諸義行。

translations.literal: The dynastic history, following earlier precedent, compiled biographies of filial piety and brotherly devotion, also treating many acts of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The dynastic history, following earlier precedent, compiled biographies of filial piety and brotherly devotion and also recorded many acts of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 合之方志甄錄、文家傳述，無慮千百人。

translations.literal: Together with selections in local gazetteers and accounts by literary families, there were no fewer than a thousand or ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Together with selections in local gazetteers and accounts by literary families, the number must run to a thousand or more.

sentences.zh: 採其尤者，用沈約宋書例，為孝義傳。

translations.literal: Choosing the most outstanding, following Shen Yue's precedent in the Book of Song, biographies of filial piety and righteousness were compiled.
translations.idiomatic: Selecting the most outstanding cases and following Shen Yue's precedent in the Book of Song, these were compiled as biographies of filial piety and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 事親存沒能盡禮；

translations.literal: Serving parents in life and death with full observance of ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Serving parents in life and death with full observance of ritual;

sentences.zh: 或遘家庭之變，能不失其正；

translations.literal: or encountering domestic upheaval, yet not losing rectitude;
translations.idiomatic: or encountering domestic upheaval yet not losing one's rectitude;

sentences.zh: 或遇寇難、值水火，能全其親。

translations.literal: or meeting bandits and calamity, fire and flood, yet preserving one's parents.
translations.idiomatic: or meeting bandits, fire, and flood yet preserving one's parents.

sentences.zh: 若殉親而死，或為親復仇，友於兄弟，同居三五世以上，及凡有義行者，各以類聚。

translations.literal: Those who died mourning parents, or avenged parents, were brotherly among siblings, dwelt together for three to five generations or more, and all who had righteous conduct were grouped each by kind.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died in mourning for their parents, who avenged their parents, who lived in harmony with brothers for three to five generations or more, and all who performed righteous deeds were grouped each according to kind.

sentences.zh: 事同，以時次。

translations.literal: When the matter was the same, they were ordered by time.
translations.idiomatic: Within each category, entries are arranged chronologically.

sentences.zh: 孝為二卷，友與義合一卷。

translations.literal: Filial piety fills two juan; brotherly devotion and righteousness share one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety occupies two scrolls; brotherly devotion and righteousness share one scroll.

sentences.zh: 硃用純，字致一，江南崑山人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yongchun, style name Zhiyi, was a native of Kunshan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yongchun, whose style was Zhiyi, was from Kunshan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父集璜，明季以諸生死難。

translations.literal: His father Jihuang died in the Ming calamity as a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jihuang, a licentiate, perished in the Ming dynasty's final crisis.

sentences.zh: 用純慕王裒攀柏之義，自號曰柏廬。

translations.literal: Yongchun admired Wang Pou's meaning in climbing the cypress and styled himself Cypress Hut.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchun admired Wang Pou's act of clinging to the cypress at his father's grave and took for himself the sobriquet Cypress Hut.

sentences.zh: 棄諸生，奉母。

translations.literal: He abandoned his licentiate status and served his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He gave up his status as a licentiate to devote himself to his mother.

sentences.zh: 其學確守程、硃，知行並進，而程於至敬。

translations.literal: His learning firmly upheld Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, advancing knowledge and action together, and he especially applied this to utmost reverence.
translations.idiomatic: His learning firmly upheld the teachings of Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi; he advanced knowledge and practice together and applied them above all to utmost reverence.

sentences.zh: 來學者授以小學、近思錄。

translations.literal: Those who came to study he taught from the Elementary Learning and Reflections on Things at Hand.
translations.idiomatic: Students who came to him he instructed in the Elementary Learning and Reflections on Things at Hand.

sentences.zh: 仿白鹿洞規，設講約，從者皆興起。

translations.literal: Imitating the White Deer Grotto regulations, he established lecture covenants, and all who followed were stirred to action.
translations.idiomatic: Following the regulations of the White Deer Grotto Academy, he established lecture covenants, and all who followed him were stirred to earnest effort.

sentences.zh: 居喪哀毀，嘗曰：「宰我欲短喪，吾黨皆以為怪，然可見古人喪禮之盡，必蔬水饘粥哭泣哀毀無苟弛。

translations.literal: In mourning he was stricken with grief and emaciation, and once said: "When Zai Wo wished to shorten mourning, our party all thought it strange, yet one can see how fully the ancients observed mourning ritual: they must have taken only vegetables and water, gruel and porridge, weeping with grief and emaciation without any careless relaxation.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he was stricken with grief and wasted away. He once said: "When Zai Wo wished to shorten the mourning period, our party all thought it strange, yet one can see how fully the ancients observed mourning ritual: they took only vegetables and water, gruel and porridge, weeping with grief and wasting away without any careless slackening.

sentences.zh: 若今人飲酒食肉不改其常，雖更三年，豈謂久哉？」

translations.literal: If people today drink wine and eat meat without changing their usual ways, even if it lasted three years more, how could that be called long?"
translations.idiomatic: If people today drink wine and eat meat without changing their usual ways, even if it went on for three years, how could that be called a long mourning?"

sentences.zh: 晚作輟講語，又為治家格言，語平易而切至。

translations.literal: In his later years he wrote Cease Lecturing Sayings and also Family Maxims for Governing the Household; the language was plain yet pointed.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he wrote Cease Lecturing Sayings and also Family Maxims for Governing the Household; the language is plain yet penetrating.

sentences.zh: 病將革，設先人位，拜於堂，告無罪，顧弟子曰：「學問在性命，事業在忠孝。」

translations.literal: When his illness was near its end, he set out the tablets of his forebears, bowed in the hall, declared himself without offense, turned to his disciples and said: "Learning lies in cultivating one's nature and fate; achievement lies in loyalty and filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: When his illness was near its end, he set out the tablets of his forebears, bowed in the hall, and declared himself without offense. Turning to his disciples he said: "Learning lies in cultivating one's nature and destiny; achievement lies in loyalty and filial piety."

sentences.zh: 乃卒。

translations.literal: Then he died.
translations.idiomatic: With that he died.

sentences.zh: 用純與徐枋、楊無咎稱「吳中三高士」，皆明季死事之孤也。

translations.literal: Yongchun together with Xu Fang and Yang Wujiu were called "the three lofty scholars of Wu," all orphans of those who died for the Ming in its final years.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchun, together with Xu Fang and Yang Wujiu, were known as "the three lofty scholars of Wu"—all sons of men who had died for the Ming in its final years.

sentences.zh: 吳蕃昌，字仲木，浙江海鹽人。

translations.literal: Wu Fanchang, style name Zhongmu, was a native of Haiyan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fanchang, whose style was Zhongmu, was from Haiyan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 父麟徵，明季死難，蕃昌事所後母查孝，居喪，水漿不入口。

translations.literal: His father Linzheng died in the Ming calamity; Fanchang served his stepmother née Zha with filial piety, and in mourning took neither water nor broth.
translations.idiomatic: His father Linzheng perished in the Ming dynasty's final crisis. Fanchang served his stepmother, Lady Zha, with filial devotion; during mourning he took neither water nor broth.

sentences.zh: 既殯，啜粥，不茹蔬果。

translations.literal: After the encoffining he sipped gruel and ate no vegetables or fruit.
translations.idiomatic: After the encoffining he took only thin gruel and ate no vegetables or fruit.

sentences.zh: 寢苫，不脫衰絰。

translations.literal: He slept on the rush mat and never removed his mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: He slept on the rush mat of mourning and never removed his hempen mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 比葬，嘔血數升，逾小祥遂卒。

translations.literal: By the time of burial he had vomited several sheng of blood; past the first anniversary of mourning he died.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of burial he had vomited several pints of blood; shortly after the first anniversary of mourning he died.

sentences.zh: 從弟謙牧，字裒仲。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Qian Mu, style name Baizhong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Qian Mu, whose style was Baizhong.

sentences.zh: 為程、硃之學。

translations.literal: He studied the learning of Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to the learning of Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 事母硃孝，居喪，杖不能起。

translations.literal: He served his mother née Zhu with filial piety; in mourning he could not rise even with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother, Lady Zhu, with filial devotion; during mourning he was so weak he could not rise even with a staff.

sentences.zh: 疾稍間，手編父遺集，复困。

translations.literal: When his illness eased slightly, he compiled his father's posthumous writings by hand, then fell ill again.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness eased slightly, he compiled his father's posthumous writings by hand, then relapsed.

sentences.zh: 治窀穸，哀動行路。

translations.literal: When he arranged the burial, his grief moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he arranged the burial, his grief moved all who passed on the road.

sentences.zh: 謙牧體素羸，益不自勝，遂卒。

translations.literal: Qian Mu's constitution had always been frail; he could bear it even less and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Mu had always been frail in constitution; he could bear the strain even less and soon died.

sentences.zh: 蕃昌、謙牧皆交於張履祥，履祥稱之。

translations.literal: Fanchang and Qian Mu were both friends of Zhang Lüxiang, who praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Fanchang and Qian Mu were both friends of Zhang Lüxiang, who spoke highly of them.

sentences.zh: 時以孝著者，復有歸安沈磊，亦履祥友也。

translations.literal: Among those famed at the time for filial piety was also Shen Lei of Gui'an, likewise a friend of Lüxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Among those famed at the time for filial piety was Shen Lei of Gui'an, who was also a friend of Lüxiang.

sentences.zh: 磊事母嚴，母不御酒肉，磊力請，終不聽。

translations.literal: Lei served his mother strictly; his mother would not partake of wine or meat, and though Lei pressed her earnestly, she would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Lei served his mother with strict devotion. His mother would not touch wine or meat, and though Lei pressed her earnestly, she would not relent.

sentences.zh: 有疾，醫為言，乃御酒肉。

translations.literal: When she fell ill, the physician spoke on her behalf, and only then did she partake of wine and meat.
translations.idiomatic: When she fell ill, the physician spoke on her behalf, and only then did she consent to wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 磊客授於外，弟子具時食，不忍食，以為母未嘗也。

translations.literal: Lei taught pupils away from home; when disciples set out his meal he could not bear to eat, thinking his mother had not yet tasted it.
translations.idiomatic: Lei taught pupils away from home. When disciples set out his meal he could not bring himself to eat, thinking his mother had not yet tasted such food.

sentences.zh: 弟子乃先以饋母，曰：「太君食矣。」

translations.literal: The disciples would first send food to his mother, then say: "The Lady has eaten."
translations.idiomatic: The disciples would first send food to his mother, then say, "Your mother has already eaten."

sentences.zh: 乃食，率以為常。

translations.literal: Only then would he eat; this became his constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: Only then would he eat. This became his constant practice.

sentences.zh: 周靖，江南吳縣人。

translations.literal: Zhou Jing was a native of Wu County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing was from Wu County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父茂蘭，刺血上書明父順昌冤，事具明史。

translations.literal: His father Maolan wrote a petition in his own blood to clear the injustice done to his father Shunchang; the matter is recorded in full in the History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maolan wrote a petition in his own blood to clear the injustice done to his father Shunchang; the full account is given in the History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 靖少補諸生，事親能盡力。

translations.literal: Jing in his youth received appointment as licentiate and served his parents with utmost effort.
translations.idiomatic: Jing received appointment as a licentiate in his youth and served his parents with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 茂蘭卒，擗踴哭泣，喪葬悉如禮。

translations.literal: When Maolan died, Jing beat his breast and stamped, weeping; the funeral and burial were entirely according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Maolan died, Jing beat his breast and wept aloud; the funeral and burial were conducted entirely according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 三年不脫衰絰，不飲酒食肉。

translations.literal: For three years he did not remove his mourning garments and drank no wine or ate no meat.
translations.idiomatic: For three years he did not remove his mourning garments and took neither wine nor meat.

sentences.zh: 小祥，有疾作，或謂在禮得飲酒食肉，靖不可。

translations.literal: At the first anniversary of mourning an illness arose; some said that by ritual he might drink wine and eat meat, but Jing would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: At the first anniversary of mourning he fell ill; some said that by ritual he might now drink wine and eat meat, but Jing would not consent.

sentences.zh: 靖素善作篆，或請題榜，亦以喪辭。

translations.literal: Jing had always been skilled at seal script; when some asked him to inscribe a placard, he also declined on grounds of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had always been skilled at seal script; when people asked him to inscribe a placard, he likewise declined on grounds of mourning.

sentences.zh: 耿燿，河南太康人。

translations.literal: Geng Yao was a native of Taikang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Yao was from Taikang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 世農。

translations.literal: His family were farmers for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been farmers for generations.

sentences.zh: 父應科，好施與，七世同居，顏其堂曰「效藝」。

translations.literal: His father Yingke was fond of giving; seven generations dwelt together, and he inscribed his hall "Emulating the Arts."
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingke was generous in giving; seven generations of the family lived together, and he inscribed his hall with the words "Emulating the Arts."

sentences.zh: 兄光，明諸生，孝後母而教諸弟嚴，燿從之學，事必諮而後行。

translations.literal: His elder brother Guang, a Ming licentiate, was filial to his stepmother and taught his younger brothers strictly; Yao studied under him and would consult before acting on any matter.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Guang, a Ming licentiate, was filial to his stepmother and taught his younger brothers with strictness. Yao studied under him and would consult Guang before acting on any matter.

sentences.zh: 明末，流寇屠太康，燿與弟炳舁母避河北，貿布以養。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming, roving bandits massacred Taikang; Yao and his younger brother Bing carried their mother on a litter to flee north of the Yellow River and traded in cloth to support her.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Ming, roving bandits ravaged Taikang. Yao and his younger brother Bing carried their mother on a litter to flee north of the Yellow River and traded in cloth to support her.

sentences.zh: 母病，朝出暮歸，不解帶累月。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, he went out at dawn and returned at dusk, not loosening his belt for many months.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he went out at dawn and returned at dusk, not loosening his belt for many months on end.

sentences.zh: 母卒，挽車歸母喪。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he drew the cart to bring her coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he himself drew the cart to bring her coffin home.

sentences.zh: 炳亦純謹，定興耿權與弟極以孝友聞，炳慕其為人，分田舍處之，孫奇逢為作三耿傳焉。

translations.literal: Bing was also pure and careful; Geng Quan of Dingxing and his younger brother Ji were famed for filial piety and brotherly devotion; Bing admired their conduct, divided fields and houses to settle them, and Sun Qifeng wrote a biography of the three Gengs.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was likewise pure and conscientious. Geng Quan of Dingxing and his younger brother Ji were renowned for filial piety and brotherly devotion; Bing admired their conduct, divided fields and houses to settle them nearby, and Sun Qifeng wrote a biography of the three Gengs.

sentences.zh: 方寇至，光前卒，未葬，子於彝號泣守其柩不去，寇執之，推隕城下，傷腰膂，幾死。

translations.literal: Just as the bandits arrived, Guang had died earlier and was not yet buried; his son Yu Yi wailed and guarded the coffin without leaving; the bandits seized him and pushed him off the city wall, injuring his loins and back, nearly killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the bandits arrived, Guang had already died and was not yet buried. His son Yu Yi wailed and guarded the coffin without leaving. The bandits seized him and pushed him off the city wall, injuring his back and loins and nearly killing him.

sentences.zh: 寇退，歸掬土掩柩乃去。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, he returned, scooped earth to cover the coffin, and only then left.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits withdrew, he returned, scooped earth to cover the coffin, and only then departed.

sentences.zh: 縣飢，知縣餽以粟，散贍貧乏。

translations.literal: When the county suffered famine, the magistrate presented him with grain, which he distributed to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: When the county suffered famine, the magistrate gave him grain, which he distributed to relieve the poor.

sentences.zh: 督僮蔬，任飢者刈以食。

translations.literal: He had his servants plant vegetables and allowed the hungry to harvest and eat.
translations.idiomatic: He had his servants plant vegetables and allowed the hungry to harvest them for food.

sentences.zh: 同時有耿輔，虞城人。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Geng Fu, a native of Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Geng Fu, from Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 奉母避寇開封，寇決河灌城，倚浮木負母以渡。

translations.literal: He supported his mother in fleeing bandits to Kaifeng; the bandits breached the Yellow River to flood the city, and leaning on a floating log he carried his mother across.
translations.idiomatic: He supported his mother in fleeing bandits to Kaifeng. When the bandits breached the Yellow River to flood the city, he leaned on a floating log and carried his mother across.

sentences.zh: 母卒，哀毀，緇衣粗食終其世。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he was stricken with grief; in black garments and coarse food he ended his days.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he was stricken with grief and spent the rest of his life in black garments and coarse food.

sentences.zh: 李景濂，字亦週，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Li Jinglian, style name Yizhou, was a native of Yin County in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglian, whose style was Yizhou, was from Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 幼喪母，父再娶於何而卒。

translations.literal: He lost his mother in childhood; his father remarried a woman of the He clan and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother in childhood. His father remarried a woman of the He clan and then died.

sentences.zh: 何年少，媒氏欲奪之，景濂聞，伺於道，出椎擊之，歸告何。

translations.literal: He was young in years; a matchmaker wished to take her away; Jinglian heard of it, waited on the road, came out with a mallet and struck the man, then returned and told Lady He.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He was still young; a matchmaker wished to take her away in marriage. When Jinglian heard of it, he waited on the road, came out with a mallet and struck the man, then returned and told Lady He.

sentences.zh: 何相與慟哭，誓相依終身。

translations.literal: Lady He together with him wept bitterly and vowed to rely on each other for life.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He wept bitterly with him, and they vowed to rely on each other for life.

sentences.zh: 何教景濂嚴，景濂事何甚謹。

translations.literal: Lady He taught Jinglian strictly, and Jinglian served Lady He with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He taught Jinglian with strictness, and Jinglian served her with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 何嗜酪，景濂日入市求之，端捧急趨，如鳥張翼。

translations.literal: Lady He loved curds; Jinglian went daily to the market to seek them, holding them level and hurrying along like a bird spreading its wings.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He loved curds; Jinglian went to the market every day to buy them, holding the bowl level and hurrying along like a bird spreading its wings.

sentences.zh: 市人怪而求其故，則皆歎其孝，為讓道。

translations.literal: Market people wondered and asked the reason; then all sighed at his filial piety and made way for him.
translations.idiomatic: People in the market wondered and asked the reason; when they learned it, all sighed at his filial piety and made way for him.

sentences.zh: 何老病，景濂侍疾七年不怠。

translations.literal: When Lady He grew old and ill, Jinglian attended her illness for seven years without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady He grew old and fell ill, Jinglian nursed her for seven years without slackening.

sentences.zh: 何卒，景濂亦六十，廬墓三年，作孺子泣。

translations.literal: When Lady He died, Jinglian was also sixty; he dwelt in a hut by the tomb for three years, weeping like a child.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady He died, Jinglian was himself sixty. He dwelt in a hut by her tomb for three years, weeping like a child.

sentences.zh: 景濂明諸生，明亡，棄諸生去為醫。

translations.literal: Jinglian had been a Ming licentiate; when the Ming fell he abandoned his licentiate status and became a physician.
translations.idiomatic: Jinglian had been a Ming licentiate; when the Ming fell he gave up that status and became a physician.

sentences.zh: 汪灝，江南休寧人。

translations.literal: Wang Hao was a native of Xiuning in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao was from Xiuning in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 晨、日昂、日昇，其弟也。

translations.literal: Chen, Ri'ang, and Risheng were his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, Ri'ang, and Risheng were his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 父病咯血，灝年十六，割股和藥進，良愈。

translations.literal: His father was ill with spitting blood; Hao at age sixteen cut flesh from his thigh, mixed it with medicine, and presented it; his father recovered fully.
translations.idiomatic: His father suffered from spitting blood. When Hao was sixteen he cut flesh from his thigh, mixed it with medicine, and gave it to his father, who recovered fully.

sentences.zh: 後數年病足，晨割股煉為末，敷治亦愈。

translations.literal: Several years later his father had an ailment of the foot; Chen cut flesh from his thigh, refined it to powder, applied it as treatment, and he also recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later his father suffered from an ailment of the foot. Chen cut flesh from his thigh, refined it to powder, applied it as treatment, and he likewise recovered.

sentences.zh: 又數年復咯血，晨复割臂以療。

translations.literal: Several years later he again spat blood; Chen again cut flesh from his arm to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later his father again spat blood; Chen again cut flesh from his arm to treat him.

sentences.zh: 更數年，疾大作，灝复割臂，勿瘳。

translations.literal: Several years later the illness grew severe; Hao again cut flesh from his arm, but there was no recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the illness grew severe. Hao again cut flesh from his arm, but his father did not recover.

sentences.zh: 晨病，日昂泣曰：「吾兄割臂愈父，吾不能割以愈吾兄乎？」

translations.literal: When Chen fell ill, Ri'ang wept and said: "My elder brother cut his arm to cure our father; can I not cut mine to cure my elder brother?"
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell ill, Ri'ang wept and said, "My elder brother cut his arm to cure our father. Can I not cut mine to cure my brother?"

sentences.zh: 眾尼之。

translations.literal: The crowd restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd restrained him.

sentences.zh: 懵且僕，匠治棺，日昇持匠斧斷指，血淋漓，調藥以飲晨。

translations.literal: Meng was also a servant; a carpenter was making a coffin; Risheng took the carpenter's axe and severed a finger, blood streaming down, mixed medicine and gave it to Chen to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was also a servant. While a carpenter was making a coffin, Risheng seized the carpenter's axe and severed a finger, blood streaming down, mixed medicine, and gave it to Chen to drink.

sentences.zh: 有司表其門曰「一門四孝友」。

translations.literal: The authorities commended their gate with the inscription "Four Filial and Brotherly Men in One Household."
translations.idiomatic: The authorities commended their household with a plaque reading "Four Filial and Brotherly Men in One Household."

sentences.zh: 錢塘吳瑗及弟琦、璠、琰相友愛，年皆逾九十。

translations.literal: Wu Yuan of Qiantang and his younger brothers Qi, Fan, and Yan were mutually affectionate; all lived past ninety.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuan of Qiantang and his younger brothers Qi, Fan, and Yan were deeply devoted to one another; all lived past ninety.

sentences.zh: 江蘇華亭姜應龍，應龍子世璜，世璜子文樞，文樞子超萃，超萃子懷權，懷權子栻，六世皆以孝行旌，人尤以為難。

translations.literal: Jiang Yinglong of Huating in Jiangsu; Yinglong's son Shihuang, Shihuang's son Wenshu, Wenshu's son Chao Cui, Chao Cui's son Huaiquan, Huaiquan's son Shi—six generations were all honored for filial conduct, which people especially regarded as difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yinglong of Huating in Jiangsu was followed by his son Shihuang, Shihuang's son Wenshu, Wenshu's son Chao Cui, Chao Cui's son Huaiquan, and Huaiquan's son Shi. Six generations in succession were honored for filial conduct, which people regarded as especially remarkable.

sentences.zh: 黃農，江南元和人。

translations.literal: Huang Nong was a native of Yuanhe in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Nong was from Yuanhe in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 父袞，諸生。

translations.literal: His father Gun was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gun was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 農年十餘，母吳病六年，農侍疾不懈。

translations.literal: When Nong was just over ten, his mother née Wu was ill for six years; Nong attended her illness without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong was just over ten, his mother Lady Wu was ill for six years; Nong nursed her without slackening.

sentences.zh: 母卒，慟屢絕，坐臥母柩側。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he was stricken with grief and repeatedly fainted, sitting and lying beside her coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he was stricken with grief and repeatedly fainted, sitting and lying beside her coffin.

sentences.zh: 袞客授於外，攜農俱。

translations.literal: Gun taught pupils away from home and took Nong along.
translations.idiomatic: Gun taught pupils away from home and took Nong with him.

sentences.zh: 久之，察其枕漬淚若膏，貌癯然如初喪。

translations.literal: After a long while he noticed his pillow soaked with tears like grease, his appearance wasted as at the first days of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he noticed Nong's pillow soaked with tears like grease and his appearance wasted as at the first days of mourning.

sentences.zh: 袞客授稍遠家，農歸，五日一往省，袞止之，則私伺門外問安否，衣服器用，時其寒暑具以往。

translations.literal: When Gun's teaching took him somewhat far from home, Nong would return and go every five days to visit; Gun forbade it, so he would secretly wait outside the gate to ask after her well-being, bringing clothing and utensils suited to the season's cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gun's teaching took him somewhat far from home, Nong would return every five days to visit his mother. Gun forbade this, so Nong would secretly wait outside the gate to ask after her well-being, bringing clothing and utensils suited to the season's cold and heat.

sentences.zh: 一夕，心悸，走省，袞得暴疾，舁以歸。

translations.literal: One night his heart palpitated; he ran to visit and found Gun stricken with sudden illness; he carried him home on a litter.
translations.idiomatic: One night his heart palpitated; he ran to visit and found Gun stricken with sudden illness. He carried him home on a litter.

sentences.zh: 會除夕禱神，原減算益父，袞愈。

translations.literal: It happened to be New Year's Eve; he prayed to the gods, vowing to shorten his own allotted span to lengthen his father's; Gun recovered.
translations.idiomatic: It happened to be New Year's Eve. He prayed to the gods, vowing to shorten his own allotted span to lengthen his father's life, and Gun recovered.

sentences.zh: 農三十餘而卒，妻金，亦賢孝。

translations.literal: Nong died in his thirties; his wife née Jin was also virtuous and filial.
translations.idiomatic: Nong died in his thirties. His wife Lady Jin was also virtuous and filial.

sentences.zh: 曹亨，陝西鎮安人。

translations.literal: Cao Heng was a native of Zhen'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Heng was from Zhen'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 年十一喪母，不能具棺，號泣於路，乞自鬻為斂。

translations.literal: At age eleven he lost his mother; unable to provide a coffin, he wailed on the road, begging to sell himself to pay for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: At age eleven he lost his mother. Unable to provide a coffin, he wailed on the road, begging to sell himself to pay for the burial.

sentences.zh: 或與之金，葬母畢，即詣其家執役終身。

translations.literal: Someone gave him gold; when his mother's burial was complete, he went at once to that man's house and served as a bondsman for life.
translations.idiomatic: Someone gave him gold. When his mother's burial was complete, he went at once to that man's house and served as a bondsman for life.

sentences.zh: 黃嘉章，湖南桂陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Jiazhang was a native of Guiyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jiazhang was from Guiyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂之亂，從父避兵連珠崖。

translations.literal: During Wu Sangui's rebellion, he followed his father in fleeing the troops to Lianzhuya.
translations.idiomatic: During Wu Sangui's rebellion, he followed his father in fleeing the troops to Lianzhuya.

sentences.zh: 父歿，兄嘉林年十六，嘉章亦年十一，自鬻以葬父。

translations.literal: When his father died, his elder brother Jialin was sixteen and Jiazhang also eleven; he sold himself to bury his father.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, his elder brother Jialin was sixteen and Jiazhang was eleven. Jiazhang sold himself to bury his father.

sentences.zh: 嘉林稍長，力為傭，得錢贖嘉章還，兄弟相友愛。

translations.literal: When Jialin grew somewhat older, he worked as a hired laborer, obtained money to redeem Jiazhang and bring him back; the brothers were mutually affectionate.
translations.idiomatic: When Jialin grew older, he worked as a hired laborer, obtained money to redeem Jiazhang and bring him home, and the brothers were deeply devoted to one another.

sentences.zh: 鄭明允，江南歙縣人。

translations.literal: Zheng Mingyun was a native of She County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mingyun was from She County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，耿精忠兵至，明允侍母抱譜牒及先世遺筆入山。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign, when Geng Jingzhong's troops arrived, Mingyun attended his mother, carrying genealogical records and his forebears' writings into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign, when Geng Jingzhong's troops arrived, Mingyun attended his mother, carrying genealogical records and his forebears' writings into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 賊大索山中，明允夜負母匿僻塢，還挈二子，未至，霧溢山，虎聲震林木，納二子石穴中，疾趨侍母。

translations.literal: The bandits searched the mountains thoroughly; Mingyun at night carried his mother to hide in a secluded ravine, then returned to bring his two sons; before he arrived, fog filled the mountains and tiger roars shook the trees; he placed the two sons in a stone cave and hurried to attend his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits searched the mountains thoroughly. Mingyun carried his mother at night to hide in a secluded ravine, then returned for his two sons. Before he reached them, fog filled the mountains and tiger roars shook the trees. He placed his sons in a stone cave and hurried back to his mother.

sentences.zh: 賊退，二子亦無恙。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, the two sons were also unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits withdrew, his two sons were also unharmed.

sentences.zh: 兄病，視湯藥不去側。

translations.literal: When his elder brother fell ill, he watched over the medicine and broth without leaving his side.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother fell ill, he watched over his medicine and broth without leaving his side.

sentences.zh: 及亡，每慟輒絕。

translations.literal: When he died, each bout of grief brought fainting.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother died, each bout of grief brought fainting.

sentences.zh: 與其戚同賈，失其貲，明允發橐金盡與之。

translations.literal: A kinsman traded with him and lost his capital; Mingyun opened his purse and gave him all he had.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman traded with him and lost his capital. Mingyun opened his purse and gave him everything he had.

sentences.zh: 族子縊客舍，明允為坐守達曙，白於官，出私財以斂。

translations.literal: A clansman's son hanged himself in a guesthouse; Mingyun sat guard until dawn, reported to the authorities, and paid from his private funds for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman's son hanged himself in a guesthouse. Mingyun sat guard until dawn, reported the matter to the authorities, and paid from his private funds for the burial.

sentences.zh: 有友盪其貲，困甚，明允罄所有佽之，無難色。

translations.literal: A friend squandered his capital and was in great distress; Mingyun gave all he possessed to help him, without any sign of reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: A friend squandered his capital and was in great distress. Mingyun gave everything he possessed to help him, without the slightest reluctance.

sentences.zh: 明允世業醫，精而不試，曰：「十得九，猶有一誤。」

translations.literal: Mingyun's family profession was medicine; he was skilled but would not practice, saying: "Nine out of ten succeed, yet there is still one mistake."
translations.idiomatic: Mingyun's family profession was medicine. He was skilled but would not practice, saying, "Nine out of ten succeed, yet there is still one mistake."

sentences.zh: 業賈終其身。

translations.literal: He traded for his entire life.
translations.idiomatic: He traded for his entire life instead.

sentences.zh: 劉宗洙，字長源；

translations.literal: Liu Zongzhu, style name Changyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhu, whose style was Changyuan;

sentences.zh: 弟恩廣，字錫三：湖北襄城人。

translations.literal: his younger brother Enguang, style name Xisan: natives of Xiangcheng in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: and his younger brother Enguang, whose style was Xisan, were from Xiangcheng in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 父漢臣，明季從軍。

translations.literal: Their father Hanchen followed the army in the Ming's final years.
translations.idiomatic: Their father Hanchen followed the army in the Ming dynasty's final years.

sentences.zh: 襄城破，被數創，幾殆。

translations.literal: When Xiangcheng fell, he received many wounds and was nearly killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangcheng fell, he received many wounds and was nearly killed.

sentences.zh: 恩廣兩耳斷，號泣負以歸。

translations.literal: Enguang's two ears were severed; he wailed and carried his father home on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Enguang's two ears were severed. He wailed and carried his father home on his back.

sentences.zh: 宗洙方走避寇，聞父難，往赴，賊截其耳鼻。

translations.literal: Zongzhu was then fleeing to escape the bandits; hearing of his father's peril, he went to rescue him, and the bandits cut off his ears and nose.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhu was then fleeing the bandits. Hearing of his father's peril, he went to rescue him, and the bandits cut off his ears and nose.

sentences.zh: 居數年，父病，嘗糞，時稱襄城「嘗糞孝子」。

translations.literal: Several years later his father fell ill; he tasted his father's stool; at the time he was called Xiangcheng's "filial son who tasted stool."
translations.idiomatic: Several years later his father fell ill. Zongzhu tasted his father's stool to test his condition and was known at the time as Xiangcheng's "filial son who tasted stool."

sentences.zh: 父歾，與季弟宗泗同居，俄與恩廣皆得官，以母老不出。

translations.literal: When his father died, he dwelt with his youngest brother Zongsi; soon both he and Enguang received official appointments, but because their mother was old they did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When their father died, Zongzhu lived with his youngest brother Zongsi. Soon both he and Enguang received official appointments, but because their mother was old they did not take office.

sentences.zh: 母歾，恩廣嘔血至篤疾。

translations.literal: When their mother died, Enguang spat blood until gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: When their mother died, Enguang spat blood until he was gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 或慰解，曰：「勿復言，五內裂矣！」

translations.literal: When some tried to comfort him, he said: "Speak no more—my five viscera are torn apart!"
translations.idiomatic: When some tried to comfort him, he said, "Speak no more—my five viscera are torn apart!"

sentences.zh: 遂卒。

translations.literal: Then he died.
translations.idiomatic: With that he died.

sentences.zh: 宗洙積哀兼痛弟，亦嘔血卒。

translations.literal: Zongzhu, grief piled upon grief for his brother, also spat blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhu, grief piled upon grief for his brother, likewise spat blood and died.

sentences.zh: 恩廣子青藜，康熙四十五年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: Enguang's son Qingli passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fifth year of Kangxi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Enguang's son Qingli passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fifth year of Kangxi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，哀毀嘔血，事母不復出。

translations.literal: When his father died he was stricken with grief and spat blood; he served his mother and did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was stricken with grief and spat blood. He devoted himself to his mother and did not take office again.

sentences.zh: 何復漢，江西廣昌人。

translations.literal: He Fuhan was a native of Guangchang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He Fuhan was from Guangchang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十五而喪父，哭淚皆血。

translations.literal: At fifteen he lost his father; his weeping tears were all blood.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he lost his father; his tears as he wept were all blood.

sentences.zh: 長事母孝，母疾作，嘗糞苦甘以測病深淺，不解帶者數月。

translations.literal: Grown, he served his mother filially; when her illness arose, he tasted her stool for bitterness or sweetness to gauge the depth of the illness, not loosening his belt for many months.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he served his mother with filial devotion. When she fell ill, he tasted her stool for bitterness or sweetness to gauge how serious the illness was, and did not loosen his belt for many months.

sentences.zh: 母歾，寢苫三月，淚漬苫左右盡血痕。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he slept on the rush mat for three months; tears soaked the mat on both sides until it was all bloodstained.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he slept on the rush mat of mourning for three months; tears soaked both sides of the mat until they were covered with bloodstains.

sentences.zh: 葬，乃廬墓側，日夜悲號，喪終猶廬居。

translations.literal: After burial he dwelt in a hut beside the tomb, wailing day and night; when mourning ended he still lived in the hut.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he dwelt in a hut beside the tomb, wailing day and night. When the mourning period ended he still lived there.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠兵至，复漢守墓不去，親知毀其廬，乃哭而行。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong's troops arrived, Fuhan guarded the tomb and would not leave; kin and friends tore down his hut, and only then did he weep and depart.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong's troops arrived, Fuhan guarded the tomb and would not leave. Kin and friends tore down his hut, and only then did he weep and depart.

sentences.zh: 著古今粹言示子孫。

translations.literal: He wrote Pure Sayings of Past and Present to instruct his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Pure Sayings of Past and Present to instruct his descendants.

sentences.zh: 子人龍，康熙五十二年進士，入翰林。

translations.literal: His son Renlong passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-second year of Kangxi and entered the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renlong passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-second year of Kangxi and entered the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 許季覺，浙江海寧人。

translations.literal: Xu Jijue was a native of Haining in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jijue was from Haining in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少尚俠，既折節讀書。

translations.literal: In youth he admired chivalry; later he restrained himself and took up study.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he admired chivalry; later he restrained himself and devoted himself to study.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，水漿不入口者七日，杖而後起。

translations.literal: During mourning for his parents he took neither water nor broth for seven days, and only rose with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his parents he took neither water nor broth for seven days and could rise only with a staff.

sentences.zh: 含殮、殯葬、虞祔、卒哭、祥禫皆用古禮。

translations.literal: Encoffining, burial, yufu, zuku, xiang, and chan all followed ancient ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Encoffining, burial, yufu, zuku, xiang, and chan were all conducted according to ancient ritual.

sentences.zh: 葬，躬負土，廬於側，朝夕哭不輟。

translations.literal: At burial he personally carried earth on his back, dwelt in a hut beside the tomb, and wept morning and evening without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial he personally carried earth on his back, dwelt in a hut beside the tomb, and wept morning and evening without cease.

sentences.zh: 季覺故與同縣查氏交密，查氏貴，營葬侵許氏墓地。

translations.literal: Jijue had been on close terms with the Zha clan of the same county; the Zha were eminent and in arranging a burial encroached on the Xu clan's grave land.
translations.idiomatic: Jijue had been on close terms with the eminent Zha clan of the same county, but when the Zha arranged a burial they encroached on the Xu clan's grave land.

sentences.zh: 季覺曰：「吾不能以友賣親。」

translations.literal: Jijue said: "I cannot sell my kin for the sake of friendship."
translations.idiomatic: Jijue said, "I cannot betray my kin for the sake of friendship."

sentences.zh: 訟連年不決，親朋居間，季覺終不讓。

translations.literal: The lawsuit dragged on for years unresolved; kin and friends mediated, but Jijue would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The lawsuit dragged on for years without resolution. Kin and friends mediated, but Jijue would not yield.

sentences.zh: 查氏誣季覺通海，逮獄，有為辨者，獄稍解，避地山陰。

translations.literal: The Zha clan accused Jijue of communicating with the sea rebels; he was arrested and imprisoned; some spoke in his defense and the case was somewhat eased; he fled to Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: The Zha clan accused Jijue of communicating with maritime rebels. He was arrested and imprisoned. Some spoke in his defense and the case was somewhat eased, and he fled to Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 查氏复誣以他事，再逮獄。

translations.literal: The Zha clan again accused him on other grounds and he was arrested and imprisoned a second time.
translations.idiomatic: The Zha clan again accused him on other grounds, and he was arrested and imprisoned a second time.

sentences.zh: 季覺度不免，獄中碎瓷盎吞之，死。

translations.literal: Jijue judged that he could not escape; in prison he smashed a porcelain bowl and swallowed the shards, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jijue judged that he could not escape. In prison he smashed a porcelain bowl, swallowed the shards, and died.

sentences.zh: 吳氏四孝子，江南崇明人，失其名。

translations.literal: The four filial sons of the Wu clan, natives of Chongming in Jiangnan, their names are lost.
translations.idiomatic: The four filial sons of the Wu clan were from Chongming in Jiangnan; their names are lost.

sentences.zh: 父壯年家貧，鬻子為富家奴。

translations.literal: Their father in his prime was poor in household; he sold his sons as slaves to a wealthy family.
translations.idiomatic: Their father, though in his prime, was poor and sold his sons as slaves to a wealthy family.

sentences.zh: 及長，皆能自贖。

translations.literal: When grown, all were able to redeem themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When they grew up, all were able to redeem themselves.

sentences.zh: 娶婦列肆居，養父母，兄弟議奉父母膳，月而易。

translations.literal: They married and wives set up shops to live by, supporting their parents; the brothers discussed providing their parents' meals, taking turns each month.
translations.idiomatic: They married, and their wives set up shops to live by while they supported their parents. The brothers discussed providing their parents' meals by taking turns each month.

sentences.zh: 諸婦曰：「翁姑老矣！

translations.literal: The daughters-in-law said: "Father-in-law and mother-in-law are old!
translations.idiomatic: The daughters-in-law said, "Father-in-law and mother-in-law are old!

sentences.zh: 月而易，必三月後方為翁姑具膳，太疏。」

translations.literal: Taking turns each month, it would be three months before it was one's turn to prepare meals for them—too infrequent."
translations.idiomatic: If we take turns each month, it will be three months before it is one's turn to prepare meals for them—that is too infrequent."

sentences.zh: 复議日而易，諸婦又曰：「翁姑老矣！

translations.literal: They discussed again, taking turns each day; the daughters-in-law again said: "Father-in-law and mother-in-law are old!
translations.idiomatic: They discussed taking turns each day instead. The daughters-in-law again said, "Father-in-law and mother-in-law are old!

sentences.zh: 日而易，必三日後方為翁姑具膳，仍太疏。」

translations.literal: Taking turns each day, it would still be three days before one prepared meals for them—still too infrequent."
translations.idiomatic: If we take turns each day, it will still be three days before it is one's turn to prepare meals for them—that is still too infrequent."

sentences.zh: 乃議伯具早餐，仲午，叔脯，次日季具早餐，周而復始。

translations.literal: They then agreed that the eldest would provide breakfast, the second lunch, the third the evening meal, and the next day the youngest would provide breakfast, cycling in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: They then agreed that the eldest would provide breakfast, the second lunch, the third the evening meal, and the next day the youngest would provide breakfast, cycling in rotation.

sentences.zh: 越五日，諸子合具饌奉父母，子孫皆侍，諸婦以次上酒食，以為常。

translations.literal: Every five days the sons together prepared a feast for their parents; descendants all attended; the daughters-in-law in turn presented wine and food—this became the custom.
translations.idiomatic: Every five days the sons together prepared a feast for their parents, with all descendants in attendance and the daughters-in-law presenting wine and food in turn. This became their custom.

sentences.zh: 室置★，兄弟各具錢五十，父食畢，取錢入市嬉，易果餌，歸畀諸孫，錢將盡，复具。

translations.literal: A jar was placed in the room; each brother contributed fifty cash; when their father had finished eating, he took the money to the market for amusement, exchanged it for fruit and sweets, and returned to give them to his grandchildren; when the money was nearly gone, they supplied more.
translations.idiomatic: They placed a jar in the room into which each brother contributed fifty cash. When their father had finished eating, he took the money to the market for amusement, bought fruit and sweets, and returned to give them to his grandchildren. When the money was nearly gone, they supplied more.

sentences.zh: 父或從博徒戲，兄弟潛以錢畀博徒，令陽負與其父以為歡。

translations.literal: When their father joined gamblers in play, the brothers secretly gave money to the gamblers, having them pretend to lose to their father for his delight.
translations.idiomatic: When their father joined gamblers in play, the brothers secretly gave money to the gamblers, having them pretend to lose to their father for his delight.

sentences.zh: 行之數十年，父母皆將百歲，奉事不衰。

translations.literal: They practiced this for several decades; both parents approached a hundred years, and their service never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: They practiced this for several decades. Both parents approached a hundred years of age, and their devotion never slackened.

sentences.zh: 陸隴其為之傳。

translations.literal: Lu Longqi wrote a biography of them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Longqi wrote a biography of them.

sentences.zh: 雷顯宗，河南陳州人。

translations.literal: Lei Xianzong was a native of Chenzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Xianzong was from Chenzhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 父病瘓，顯宗摩掌熱拊父四支，二十七晝夜不倦，父良愈。

translations.literal: His father was ill with paralysis; Xianzong rubbed his palms warm and stroked his father's four limbs for twenty-seven days and nights without tiring; his father recovered fully.
translations.idiomatic: His father was ill with paralysis. Xianzong rubbed his palms warm and stroked his father's limbs for twenty-seven days and nights without tiring, and his father recovered fully.

sentences.zh: 居數年，复病劇，侍湯藥兩月餘，竟卒，哀毀柴立。

translations.literal: Several years later he fell gravely ill again; Xianzong attended the medicine and broth for more than two months; he ultimately died, and Xianzong was stricken with grief, wasted as a stick.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later his father fell gravely ill again. Xianzong attended him with medicine and broth for more than two months, but he ultimately died. Xianzong was stricken with grief and wasted away like a stick.

sentences.zh: 居母喪亦如之。

translations.literal: In mourning for his mother he was the same.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his mother he was the same.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，歲饑，出米粟濟貧乏，代償其逋賦。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign, in years of famine he gave out grain to relieve the poor and paid their overdue taxes on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign, in years of famine he gave out grain to relieve the poor and paid their overdue taxes on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 有鬻其孥者，贖以歸。

translations.literal: When some sold their wives and children, he redeemed them and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: When some sold their wives and children, he redeemed them and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 佽婚葬者三百餘家。

translations.literal: He assisted with weddings and funerals for more than three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted with weddings and funerals for more than three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 顯宗年九十，朔望集家人講孝經、曲禮、內則諸篇，裡閈稱其家範。

translations.literal: Xianzong at age ninety gathered his family on the new and full moon to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Qu Li, the Nei Ze, and other chapters; neighbors praised his household standards.
translations.idiomatic: At ninety Xianzong gathered his family on the new and full moon to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, the Qu Li, the Nei Ze, and other chapters. Neighbors praised his household as a model.

sentences.zh: 趙清，山東諸城人。

translations.literal: Zhao Qing was a native of Zhucheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qing was from Zhucheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 生有至性，嗜酒，與同縣李澄中、劉翼明輩遍陟縣中山，縱飲，輒沉頓。

translations.literal: By nature he had utmost sincerity and loved wine; with Li Chengzhong, Liu Yiming, and others of the same county he climbed all the hills of the county, drinking freely, and always sank into stupor.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was deeply sincere and loved wine. With Li Chengzhong, Liu Yiming, and others of the same county he climbed all the hills of the county, drinking freely until he sank into stupor.

sentences.zh: 喪父，廬墓側百日，母往攜以歸。

translations.literal: When his father died, he dwelt in a hut beside the tomb for a hundred days; his mother went and brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he dwelt in a hut beside the tomb for a hundred days until his mother came and brought him home.

sentences.zh: 喪母，复廬墓側，麻衣躬畚鍤，負土為墳，毀幾殆。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he again dwelt beside the tomb, in hemp garments personally wielding basket and spade, carrying earth on his back to build the mound, his grief nearly killing him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he again dwelt beside the tomb. In hemp garments he personally wielded basket and spade, carrying earth on his back to build the mound, his grief nearly killing him.

sentences.zh: 客有勸者，清曰：「清所以為此者，蓋下愚居喪法耳。

translations.literal: A guest tried to dissuade him; Qing said: "The reason Qing does this is simply the method of mourning for the lowest dullard.
translations.idiomatic: A guest tried to dissuade him. Qing said, "The reason I do this is simply the method of mourning for the lowest dullard.

sentences.zh: 清狂盪如湍水，不居墓側，將食旨，久而甘；

translations.literal: Qing is wild and unrestrained as rushing water; if I do not dwell beside the tomb, I will eat delicacies and in time find them sweet;
translations.idiomatic: I am wild and unrestrained as rushing water. If I do not dwell beside the tomb, I will eat delicacies and in time find them sweet;

sentences.zh: 聞樂，久而樂；

translations.literal: hear music and in time take pleasure in it;
translations.idiomatic: hear music and in time take pleasure in it;

sentences.zh: 居處，且久而安。

translations.literal: dwell in comfort and in time grow content.
translations.idiomatic: dwell in comfort and in time grow content.

sentences.zh: 不一期，沉湎不可問矣。

translations.literal: Before a year is out, I will be sunk in indulgence beyond recall.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year is out, I will be sunk in indulgence beyond recall.

sentences.zh: 不孝孰甚！」

translations.literal: What could be more unfilial than that!"
translations.idiomatic: What could be more unfilial than that!"

sentences.zh: 居廬久，或傳有狼與犬為守廬，狎不相齧也。

translations.literal: He dwelt in the hut for a long while; it was said that a wolf and a dog guarded the hut together, familiar with each other and not biting.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt in the hut for a long while. People said that a wolf and a dog guarded the hut together, familiar with each other and not biting one another.

sentences.zh: 榮漣，江南無錫人。

translations.literal: Rong Lian was a native of Wuxi in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lian was from Wuxi in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少孤，多病，母令為道士。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and often ill, his mother had him become a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and often ill, his mother had him become a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 善詩畫。

translations.literal: He was skilled in poetry and painting.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in poetry and painting.

sentences.zh: 事母孝，出游得珍玩、良藥必以奉母。

translations.literal: He served his mother filially; when traveling he obtained rare curios or fine medicines, he always presented them to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother with filial devotion. Whenever he traveled and obtained rare curios or fine medicines, he always presented them to his mother.

sentences.zh: 遊倦歸，晨昏侍母側。

translations.literal: When weary of travel he returned and attended his mother morning and evening at her side.
translations.idiomatic: When weary of travel he returned and attended his mother morning and evening at her side.

sentences.zh: 母卒，廬墓不復出。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he dwelt in a hut by the tomb and never went out again.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he dwelt in a hut by her tomb and never went out again.

sentences.zh: 漣與縣人杜詔及僧妙复號「三逸」。

translations.literal: Lian together with Du Zhao of the county and the monk Miao Fu were styled "the Three Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: Lian, together with Du Zhao of the county and the monk Miao Fu, were known as "the Three Recluses."

sentences.zh: 薛文，江南和州人。

translations.literal: Xue Wen was a native of Hezhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wen was from Hezhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 弟化禮。

translations.literal: His younger brother Huali.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Huali.

sentences.zh: 貧，有母，兄弟一出為傭，一留侍母，迭相代。

translations.literal: Poor, they had a mother; one brother went out as a hired laborer while one remained to serve their mother, taking turns.
translations.idiomatic: They were poor and had a mother to support. One brother went out as a hired laborer while the other remained to serve her, taking turns.

sentences.zh: 留者在母側絮絮與母語，不使孤坐。

translations.literal: The one who remained chattered at his mother's side so she would not sit alone.
translations.idiomatic: The one who remained chattered at his mother's side so she would not sit alone.

sentences.zh: 日旰，傭者還，挾酒米魚肉治食奉母，兄弟舞躍歌謳以侑。

translations.literal: At day's end the hired laborer returned, bringing wine, rice, fish, and meat to prepare food for their mother; the brothers danced and sang to entertain her.
translations.idiomatic: At day's end the hired laborer returned, bringing wine, rice, fish, and meat to prepare food for their mother. The brothers danced and sang to entertain her.

sentences.zh: 寒，負母曝戶外，兄弟前後為侏儒作態博母笑。

translations.literal: In cold weather they carried their mother outdoors to sun her; the brothers before and behind played dwarfs and made faces to amuse their mother.
translations.idiomatic: In cold weather they carried their mother outdoors to sun her. The brothers before and behind played dwarfs and made faces to amuse her.

sentences.zh: 母篤老，病且死，治殯葬畢，毀不能出戶。

translations.literal: Their mother was very old, fell ill and was near death; when the funeral arrangements were complete, their grief was such that they could not leave the house.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother was very old, fell ill, and was near death. When the funeral arrangements were complete, their grief was such that they could not leave the house.

sentences.zh: 傭主跡至家，文與化禮骨立不能起，哭益哀，數日皆死，時康熙四十二年也。

translations.literal: Their employer traced them to the house; Wen and Huali were wasted to bone and could not rise, weeping ever more bitterly; within several days both died—it was the forty-second year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Their employer traced them to the house. Wen and Huali were wasted to skin and bone and could not rise, weeping ever more bitterly. Within several days both died. It was the forty-second year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 知州何偉表其閭。

translations.literal: Prefect He Wei commended them in their neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect He Wei commended them in their neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 偉勤於民，卒，民祠焉。

translations.literal: Wei was diligent for the people; when he died, the people erected a shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was diligent in serving the people. When he died, the people erected a shrine to him.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，學政硃筠令以文、化禮附韋祠。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign, Educational Commissioner Zhu Yun ordered that Wen and Huali be enshrined alongside Wei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign, Educational Commissioner Zhu Yun ordered that Wen and Huali be enshrined alongside Wei.

sentences.zh: 曹孝童，江南無錫人。

translations.literal: Cao Xiaotong was a native of Wuxi in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiaotong was from Wuxi in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 居南郭，父為圬者。

translations.literal: He lived in the southern ward; his father was a plasterer.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in the southern ward. His father was a plasterer.

sentences.zh: 童五歲，父或扃戶出，則竟日不食。

translations.literal: When Tong was five, if his father bolted the door and went out, he would not eat all day.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong was five, if his father bolted the door and went out, he would not eat all day.

sentences.zh: 鄰或哺之，泣不食，俟父歸同食。

translations.literal: Neighbors sometimes fed him; he wept and would not eat, waiting for his father to return and eat together.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors sometimes fed him, but he wept and would not eat, waiting for his father to return so they could eat together.

sentences.zh: 父死，童嗚咽匍匐死父側，鄰市棺為斂。

translations.literal: When his father died, Tong sobbed and crawled to die beside his father; neighbors bought a coffin for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, Tong sobbed and crawled to die beside his father. Neighbors bought a coffin for the burial.

sentences.zh: 丁履豫，江南婁縣人。

translations.literal: Ding Lüyu was a native of Lou County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Lüyu was from Lou County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he served his mother filially.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he served his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 兄二、弟一皆出遊，以歲所入畀履豫，使營甘旨。

translations.literal: Two elder brothers and one younger brother all traveled away, giving their yearly earnings to Lüyu to provide delicacies for their mother.
translations.idiomatic: Two elder brothers and one younger brother all traveled away, giving their yearly earnings to Lüyu to provide delicacies for their mother.

sentences.zh: 母卒將斂，畫師貌母像絕肖，履豫諦視久之，大慟，僕地遽絕。

translations.literal: When his mother died and was about to be encoffined, a painter's portrait of his mother was utterly lifelike; Lüyu gazed at it long and intently, was stricken with great grief, fell prostrate, and suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died and was about to be encoffined, a painter's portrait of her was utterly lifelike. Lüyu gazed at it long and intently, was stricken with great grief, fell prostrate, and suddenly died.

sentences.zh: 鍾保，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Zhong Bao was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Bao was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父希晉，以步軍校從討吳三桂，積功當遷，鍾保以父老，力勸請休奉養。

translations.literal: His father Xijin, as a foot-soldier corporal, followed the campaign against Wu Sangui; having accumulated merit he was due for promotion, but Zhong Bao, because his father was old, earnestly urged him to request retirement and support him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xijin, as a foot-soldier corporal, followed the campaign against Wu Sangui. Having accumulated merit he was due for promotion, but Zhong Bao, because his father was old, earnestly urged him to request retirement and devote himself to supporting him.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，自刑部筆帖式累遷刑部郎中，居父喪哀慟，水漿不入口。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign, from a clerk in the Board of Punishments he rose in succession to director in the Board of Punishments; in mourning for his father he was stricken with grief and took neither water nor broth.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he rose from a clerk in the Board of Punishments to director in that board. In mourning for his father he was stricken with grief and took neither water nor broth.

sentences.zh: 事母尤謹，歸必侍母側。

translations.literal: He served his mother with especial care; whenever he returned he attended at her side.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother with especial care. Whenever he returned home he attended at her side.

sentences.zh: 兄盪產，撫其孤，祖遺田宅悉推與之。

translations.literal: His elder brother squandered the family property; he raised the orphans and gave over all the fields and houses inherited from their grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother squandered the family property. Zhong Bao raised the orphans and gave over all the fields and houses inherited from their grandfather.

sentences.zh: 弟貧，週之甚力。

translations.literal: His younger brother was poor; he aided him with great effort.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was poor, and he aided him with great effort.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，舉孝子，賜金，旌其門。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng he was recommended as a filial son, granted gold, and his gate was commended.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongzheng he was recommended as a filial son, granted gold, and his household was commended.

sentences.zh: 官至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose to vice minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 覺羅色爾岱，滿洲鑲紅旗人，德世庫七世孫也。

translations.literal: Jueluo Se'erdai was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner, a seventh-generation descendant of Deshiku.
translations.idiomatic: Jueluo Se'erdai was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner and a seventh-generation descendant of Deshiku.

sentences.zh: 性篤孝。

translations.literal: By nature he was deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was deeply filial.

sentences.zh: 年十七，父病，醫不效，乃割左臂為糜以進，病稍間，旋歾。

translations.literal: At age seventeen his father fell ill; medicine was ineffective, so he cut flesh from his left arm, made it into a gruel, and presented it; the illness eased slightly, then his father soon died.
translations.idiomatic: At age seventeen his father fell ill. When medicine proved ineffective, he cut flesh from his left arm, made it into a gruel, and gave it to his father. The illness eased slightly, but his father soon died.

sentences.zh: 事母益謹，母病飲食減，亦減飲食；

translations.literal: He served his mother with even greater care; when his mother fell ill and ate less, he also ate less;
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother with even greater care. When his mother fell ill and ate less, he also ate less;

sentences.zh: 飲食不能進，憂之，亦輟飲食；

translations.literal: when she could not take food, he worried and also ceased eating;
translations.idiomatic: when she could not take food, he worried and also ceased eating;

sentences.zh: 母能飲食，乃復常。

translations.literal: when his mother could eat again, he returned to normal.
translations.idiomatic: when his mother could eat again, he returned to normal.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，命舉忠孝節義，以色爾岱應，詔賜白金，旌其門，授銀庫主事，勤其官，遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng an order went out to recommend men of loyalty, filial piety, chastity, and righteousness; Se'erdai was put forward; an edict granted white silver and commended his gate; he was appointed director of the silver treasury, diligent in office, and promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng an order went out to recommend men of loyalty, filial piety, chastity, and righteousness. Se'erdai was put forward. An edict granted him white silver and commended his household. He was appointed director of the silver treasury, served diligently, and was promoted to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，以割臂療親旌者，有翁杜、佟良，與色爾岱同時有克什布。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi reign, those commended for cutting the arm to cure a parent included Weng Du and Tongliang; contemporary with Se'erdai there was also Keshibu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign, those commended for cutting the arm to cure a parent included Weng Du and Tongliang. Contemporary with Se'erdai there was also Keshibu.

sentences.zh: 翁杜，滿洲鑲白旗人；

translations.literal: Weng Du was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner;
translations.idiomatic: Weng Du was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner;

sentences.zh: 佟良，蒙古鑲黃旗人：官防禦。

translations.literal: Tongliang was a Mongol of the Bordered Yellow Banner: he held the office of garrison defense commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Tongliang was a Mongol of the Bordered Yellow Banner and held the office of garrison defense commandant.

sentences.zh: 克什布，滿洲鑲紅旗人，官三等侍衛。

translations.literal: Keshibu was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner, holding the office of third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Keshibu was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner and held the office of third-rank bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 王麟瑞，福建南靖人。

translations.literal: Wang Linrui was a native of Nanjing in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Linrui was from Nanjing in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 八歲喪母，事後母如所生。

translations.literal: He lost his mother at eight and served his stepmother as if she were his own mother.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at eight and served his stepmother as if she were his own mother.

sentences.zh: 母病暍，非時思食梅，麟瑞繞樹呼號，不食三日，梅夜華，結實奉母，母良愈。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill from heatstroke and out of season longed to eat plums, Linrui circled the tree calling out, not eating for three days; the plum tree blossomed at night and bore fruit, which he presented to his mother, and she recovered fully.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill from heatstroke and out of season longed to eat plums, Linrui circled the tree calling out and did not eat for three days. The plum tree blossomed at night and bore fruit, which he presented to his mother, and she recovered fully.

sentences.zh: 父喪，廬墓三年，遇虎，虎為卻避。

translations.literal: When his father died, he dwelt in a hut by the tomb for three years; he met a tiger, and the tiger withdrew and avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he dwelt in a hut by the tomb for three years. He met a tiger, and the tiger withdrew and avoided him.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，詔舉孝廉方正，縣以麟瑞上。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng an edict ordered recommendation of filial and incorrupt candidates; the county submitted Linrui.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongzheng an edict ordered recommendation of filial and incorrupt candidates, and the county submitted Linrui.

sentences.zh: 四年，授陝西道監察御史，出為直隸永平知府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed investigating censor of the Shaanxi Circuit and later served as prefect of Yongping in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed investigating censor of the Shaanxi Circuit and later served as prefect of Yongping in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 李盛山，福建羅源人。

translations.literal: Li Shengshan was a native of Luoyuan in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shengshan was from Luoyuan in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 母病，割肝以救，傷重，卒。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, he cut out his liver to save her; the wound was severe and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he cut out his liver to save her. The wound was severe and he died.

sentences.zh: 巡撫常賚疏請旌，下禮部，禮部議輕生愚孝，無旌表之例。

translations.literal: Governor Chang Gai memorialized requesting commendation; the matter was referred to the Board of Rites, which deliberated that harming one's life in foolish filial piety had no precedent for commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chang Gai memorialized requesting commendation. The matter was referred to the Board of Rites, which ruled that harming one's life in foolish filial piety had no precedent for commendation.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年三月壬子，世宗諭曰：「朕惟世祖、聖祖臨御萬方，立教明倫，與人為善。

translations.literal: On renzi, the third month of the sixth year of Yongzheng, the Shizong Emperor instructed: "We consider that the Founding Emperor and the Sagely Ancestor ruled the myriad regions, established instruction and clarified human relations, and did good for others.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, the third month of the sixth year of Yongzheng, the Yongzheng Emperor instructed: "We consider that the Founding Emperor and the Sagely Ancestor ruled the myriad regions, established instruction and clarified human relations, and did good for others.

sentences.zh: 而於例慎予旌表者，誠天地好生之盛心，聖人覺世之至道，視人命為至重，不可以愚昧誤戕；

translations.literal: Yet in precedent they were cautious in granting commendation—truly the great heart of Heaven and Earth that loves life, the utmost Way of the sage who awakens the world, regarding human life as supremely important and not permitting it to be mistakenly destroyed through ignorance;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in precedent they were cautious in granting commendation. This truly reflects the great heart of Heaven and Earth that loves life, the utmost Way of the sage who awakens the world, regarding human life as supremely important and not permitting it to be mistakenly destroyed through ignorance;

sentences.zh: 念孝道為至弘，不可以毀傷為正。

translations.literal: bearing in mind that filial piety is supremely vast and cannot take self-destruction as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: bearing in mind that filial piety is supremely vast and cannot take self-destruction as the standard.

sentences.zh: 但有司未嘗以聖賢經常之道，與國家愛養之心，明白宣示，是以愚夫愚婦救親而捐軀，殉夫而殞命，往往有之。

translations.literal: But officials have never clearly proclaimed the constant Way of the sages and worthies together with the state's heart of cherishing and nurturing, and so foolish men and foolish women who sacrifice their bodies to save parents or die with their husbands are often found.
translations.idiomatic: But officials have never clearly proclaimed the constant Way of the sages and worthies together with the state's heart of cherishing and nurturing the people. For this reason foolish men and foolish women who sacrifice their bodies to save parents or die with their husbands are often found.

sentences.zh: 既有其事，若不予以旌表，無以彰其苦志。
