translations.literal: Since such cases exist, if commendation is not granted, there is no way to manifest their bitter resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Since such cases exist, if commendation is not granted, there is no way to honor their bitter resolve.

sentences.zh: 故數十年來雖未定例，仍許奏聞，且有邀恩於常格之外者。

translations.literal: Therefore for several decades, though no fixed precedent was established, memorials were still permitted, and some even received favor beyond the ordinary standard.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore for several decades, though no fixed precedent was established, memorials were still permitted, and some even received favor beyond the ordinary standard.

sentences.zh: 聖祖哀矜下民之盛心，如是其周詳而委曲也。

translations.literal: The Sagely Ancestor's great heart of compassion for the common people was thus thorough and considerate in every detail.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor's great heart of compassion for the common people was thus thorough and considerate in every detail.

sentences.zh: 父母愛子，無所不至，若因己病而致其子割肝刲股以充飲饌、和湯藥，縱其子無恙，父母未有不驚憂惻怛慘惕而不安者，況因此而傷生，豈父母所忍聞乎？

translations.literal: Parents love their children without limit; if because of their own illness their child cuts out the liver or flesh from the thigh to serve as food or mix with medicine, even if the child is unharmed, what parent would not be startled, grieved, distressed, fearful, and ill at ease? How much less could they bear to hear of the child's life being harmed thereby?
translations.idiomatic: Parents love their children without limit. If because of their own illness their child cuts out the liver or flesh from the thigh to serve as food or mix with medicine, even if the child is unharmed, what parent would not be startled, grieved, distressed, fearful, and ill at ease? How much less could they bear to hear of the child's life being harmed thereby?

sentences.zh: 父母有疾，固人子盡心竭力之時，儻能至誠純孝，必且感天地、動鬼神，不必以驚世駭俗之為，著奇於日用倫常之外。

translations.literal: When parents are ill, it is indeed the time for children to exhaust heart and strength; if one can be utterly sincere and purely filial, Heaven and Earth will surely be moved and ghosts and spirits stirred—there is no need for acts that startle the world and shock custom, seeking marvels beyond daily human relations.
translations.idiomatic: When parents are ill, it is indeed the time for children to exhaust heart and strength. If one can be utterly sincere and purely filial, Heaven and Earth will surely be moved and ghosts and spirits stirred. There is no need for acts that startle the world and shock custom, seeking marvels beyond daily human relations.

sentences.zh: 婦人從一之義，醮而不改，乃天下之正道，然烈婦難，節婦尤難。

translations.literal: A woman's duty of following one husband, marrying once and not changing, is the correct Way under Heaven; yet a heroic chaste woman is hard to be, and a chaste widow is especially hard.
translations.idiomatic: A woman's duty of following one husband, marrying once and not changing, is the correct Way under Heaven. Yet a heroic chaste woman is hard to be, and a chaste widow is especially hard.

sentences.zh: 夫亡之後，婦職之當盡者更多，上有翁姑，則當代為奉養。

translations.literal: After the husband's death, a woman's duties that ought to be fulfilled are even more numerous; if there are parents-in-law above, she should support them in their place.
translations.idiomatic: After the husband's death, a woman's duties that ought to be fulfilled are even more numerous. If there are parents-in-law above, she should support them in his place.

sentences.zh: 他如修治蘋蘩，經理家業，其事難以悉數，安得以一死畢其責乎？

translations.literal: Other matters such as preparing offerings and managing the household cannot all be enumerated—how could one discharge one's responsibilities with death alone?
translations.idiomatic: Other matters such as preparing offerings and managing the household cannot all be enumerated. How could one discharge one's responsibilities with death alone?

sentences.zh: 朕今特頒訓諭，有司廣為宣示，俾知孝子節婦，自有常經，倫常之地，皆合中庸，以毋負國家教養矜全之德。

translations.literal: We now specially issue this instruction for officials to proclaim widely, so that filial sons and chaste women may know they have their constant standards, and that in the realm of human relations all should accord with the Mean, so as not to fail the state's virtue of cherishing, nurturing, and preserving life.
translations.idiomatic: We now specially issue this instruction for officials to proclaim widely, so that filial sons and chaste women may know they have their constant standards, and that in the realm of human relations all should accord with the Mean, so as not to fail the state's virtue of cherishing, nurturing, and preserving life.

sentences.zh: 倘訓諭之後，仍有不愛軀命，蹈於危亡者，朕亦不概加旌表，以成激烈輕生之習也。」

translations.literal: If after this instruction there are still those who do not cherish their lives and rush into peril and death, We also will not commend them indiscriminately, lest the practice of fierce and reckless self-destruction be encouraged."
translations.idiomatic: If after this instruction there are still those who do not cherish their lives and rush into peril and death, We also will not commend them indiscriminately, lest the practice of fierce and reckless self-destruction be encouraged."

sentences.zh: 盛山仍予旌表。

translations.literal: Shengshan was still granted commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Shengshan was still granted commendation.

sentences.zh: 李悃，河南開封府人，失其縣。

translations.literal: Li Kun was a native of Kaifeng Prefecture in Henan; his county is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kun was from Kaifeng Prefecture in Henan; his county is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 貧為木工，父病痺，奉侍惟謹。

translations.literal: Poor, he worked as a carpenter; his father was ill with paralysis and he served him with sole care.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he worked as a carpenter. His father suffered from paralysis, and he served him with sole care.

sentences.zh: 歲歉，不能養，乃行乞於市，歸啖父。

translations.literal: In years of famine he could not support him and went begging in the market, returning to feed his father.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine he could not support his father and went begging in the market, returning to feed him.

sentences.zh: 後得賑穀一石，慮不能繼，日舂升許供父，而以秕自咽。

translations.literal: Later he received a shi of relief grain; fearing it would not last, each day he husked a sheng or so for his father and swallowed the chaff himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received a shi of relief grain. Fearing it would not last, each day he husked a sheng or so for his father and swallowed the chaff himself.

sentences.zh: 父病劇，夜中鄰人時聞悃撫摩嗟泣聲，遲明則悃抱父足死矣，父亦一慟而絕。

translations.literal: When his father's illness grew severe, neighbors at night sometimes heard Kun stroking and sighing and weeping; at dawn Kun was found embracing his father's feet, dead; his father also died in one burst of grief.
translations.idiomatic: When his father's illness grew severe, neighbors at night sometimes heard Kun stroking him, sighing and weeping. At dawn Kun was found embracing his father's feet, dead. His father also died in one burst of grief.

sentences.zh: 鄰人愍其孝，收而葬之。

translations.literal: Neighbors pitied his filial piety, gathered them up, and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors pitied their filial devotion, gathered them up, and buried them.

sentences.zh: 奚緝營，字聖輝，江蘇寶山人。

translations.literal: Xi Jiying, style name Shenghui, was a native of Baoshan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jiying, whose style was Shenghui, was from Baoshan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父士本，以孝旌。

translations.literal: His father Shiben had been commended for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shiben had been commended for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 緝營幼讀論語，至「父母之年，不可不知」，輒隕涕簌簌，師奇之，謂真孝子子也。

translations.literal: Jiying in youth read the Analects; when he came to "the years of one's parents must not be unknown," tears always fell in streams; his teacher marveled and said he was truly a filial son.
translations.idiomatic: Jiying in youth read the Analects. When he came to "the years of one's parents must not be unknown," tears always fell in streams. His teacher marveled and said he was truly a filial son.

sentences.zh: 母病，刲臂以療。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, he cut flesh from his arm to treat her.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he cut flesh from his arm to treat her.

sentences.zh: 士本老，惡寒，緝營夜抱父足眠，以為常。

translations.literal: Shiben grew old and hated the cold; Jiying at night embraced his father's feet to sleep—this became his constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: Shiben grew old and hated the cold. Jiying at night embraced his father's feet to sleep—this became his constant practice.

sentences.zh: 兩弟早卒，撫其孤如所生。

translations.literal: Two younger brothers died young; he raised their orphans as if they were his own.
translations.idiomatic: Two younger brothers died young. He raised their orphans as if they were his own.

sentences.zh: 女兄嫁而貧，從妹寡，皆依以居，為營婚嫁。

translations.literal: An elder sister married into poverty; a cousin was widowed; all relied on him to live, and he arranged their marriages.
translations.idiomatic: An elder sister married into poverty and a cousin was widowed. All relied on him to live, and he arranged their marriages.

sentences.zh: 周士晉，江蘇嘉定人。

translations.literal: Zhou Shijin was a native of Jiading in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shijin was from Jiading in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 母病久，醫言惟飲人乳可生，士晉子生方九月，謀於妻李，棄道旁，以乳乳母。

translations.literal: His mother had been ill long; the physician said only human milk could save her; Shijin's son was just born in the ninth month; he consulted his wife Lady Li, abandoned the child by the roadside, and used the milk to nurse his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been ill for a long time. The physician said only human milk could save her. Shijin's son was just born in the ninth month. He consulted his wife Lady Li, abandoned the child by the roadside, and used the milk to nurse his mother.

sentences.zh: 母病已，問兒，以殤對，後李不復姙，亦無怨。

translations.literal: When his mother's illness ended, she asked after the child; he answered that the infant had died; later Lady Li bore no more children and bore no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother's illness ended, she asked after the child. He answered that the infant had died. Later Lady Li bore no more children and bore no resentment.

sentences.zh: 越十二年，有僧為殷氏子推命，年月日與士晉兒同，詰之，則得諸道旁者也，父子得復合。

translations.literal: Twelve years later a monk cast the horoscope for a son of the Yin clan; the year, month, and day matched Shijin's son; on inquiry it was the one found by the roadside; father and son were reunited.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years later a monk cast the horoscope for a son of the Yin clan. The year, month, and day matched Shijin's son. On inquiry it proved to be the child found by the roadside, and father and son were reunited.

sentences.zh: 黃有則，湖南邵陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Youze was a native of Shaoyang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Youze was from Shaoyang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 四歲喪父，母孫劬苦育以長。

translations.literal: He lost his father at four; his mother née Sun toiled bitterly to raise him.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at four. His mother Lady Sun toiled bitterly to raise him.

sentences.zh: 遣就傅，或迂之，孫曰：「吾忍死，不欲兒廢學也。」

translations.literal: She sent him to study; when the journey was long, Lady Sun said: "I endure death itself and do not wish my son to abandon his studies."
translations.idiomatic: She sent him to study. When the journey was long, Lady Sun said, "I would endure death itself rather than let my son abandon his studies."

sentences.zh: 有則大感慟，奮學，客授養母。

translations.literal: Youze was deeply moved and grieved, studied with ardor, and taught pupils away from home to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Youze was deeply moved and grieved, studied with ardor, and taught pupils away from home to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 夏無帳，主人以進，命撤之，曰：「吾母無此也。」

translations.literal: In summer he had no mosquito net; his host offered one; he ordered it removed, saying: "My mother has none of this."
translations.idiomatic: In summer he had no mosquito net. His host offered one, but he ordered it removed, saying, "My mother has none of this."

sentences.zh: 寒為製棉衣，又卻之，曰：「家貧，無以暖母，不忍享奇溫。」

translations.literal: In cold weather a padded coat was made for him; he again refused it, saying: "Our household is poor and cannot warm my mother; I cannot bear to enjoy exceptional warmth."
translations.idiomatic: In cold weather a padded coat was made for him. He again refused it, saying, "Our household is poor and cannot warm my mother. I cannot bear to enjoy exceptional warmth."

sentences.zh: 一夕風雪，既寐，復起，行三十里歸省母。

translations.literal: One night in wind and snow, after he had fallen asleep he rose again and walked thirty li to return and visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: One night in wind and snow, after he had fallen asleep he rose again and walked thirty li to return and visit his mother.

sentences.zh: 母喜曰：「吾正思兒。」

translations.literal: His mother said with joy: "I was just thinking of you."
translations.idiomatic: His mother said with joy, "I was just thinking of you."

sentences.zh: 是時母逾九十，有則亦六十矣。

translations.literal: At that time his mother was past ninety, and Youze was also sixty.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his mother was past ninety, and Youze was also sixty.

sentences.zh: 母喪，以毀卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he died from grief.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he died from grief.

sentences.zh: 王尚毅，陝西郃陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Shangyi was a native of Heyang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shangyi was from Heyang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 為人傭。

translations.literal: He worked as a hired hand.
translations.idiomatic: He worked as a hired laborer.

sentences.zh: 母佞佛，欲鑿山造佛像，力不逮，將死，以命尚毅。

translations.literal: His mother was devoted to Buddhism and wished to carve a mountain to make Buddha images; her strength could not accomplish it; as she was about to die, she charged Shangyi with the task.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was devoted to Buddhism and wished to carve a mountain to make Buddha images, but her strength was not equal to the task. As she was dying, she charged Shangyi with fulfilling her wish.

sentences.zh: 尚毅傭，嗇衣食積錢，買山闢洞，琢石為佛像，洞六，像十二，皆手造。

translations.literal: Shangyi hired himself out, stinting on food and clothing to save money, bought a mountain and opened caves, carved stone into Buddha images—six caves and twelve images, all made by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyi hired himself out, stinting on food and clothing to save money. He bought a mountain and opened caves, carving stone into Buddha images—six caves and twelve images, all made by his own hand.

sentences.zh: 或愍而助之，謝曰：「力不己出，非敬母命也。」

translations.literal: Some pitied him and offered help; he declined, saying: "If the effort is not entirely my own, it would not be honoring my mother's charge."
translations.idiomatic: Some pitied him and offered help. He declined, saying: "If the effort is not entirely my own, it would not be honoring my mother's charge."

sentences.zh: 錢盡乃輟，復出傭，得錢更為之，如是三十餘年。

translations.literal: When the money was exhausted he would stop, go out to hire himself again, and when he had money resume the work; thus for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: When the money was exhausted he would stop, go out to hire himself again, and when he had money resume the work. He did this for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 山植柏，圍以紫荊，洞上下蒔迎春，洞成方冬，花盡開，山人怪之，名曰九華洞。

translations.literal: On the mountain he planted cypresses, surrounded them with redbud; above and below the caves he planted winter jasmine; when the caves were completed it was still winter, yet the flowers all bloomed—the mountain people marveled and named it Jiuhua Cave.
translations.idiomatic: On the mountain he planted cypresses and surrounded them with redbud. Above and below the caves he planted winter jasmine. When the caves were completed it was still winter, yet the flowers all bloomed. The mountain people marveled and named it Jiuhua Cave.

sentences.zh: 山無水，鑿池而雨至，遂不涸，名曰青龍池。

translations.literal: The mountain had no water; he carved a pool and when rain came it never dried up; he named it Qinglong Pool.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain had no water. He carved a pool, and when rain came it never dried up. He named it Qinglong Pool.

sentences.zh: 胡锳，浙江上虞人。

translations.literal: Hu Ying was a native of Shangyu in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying was from Shangyu in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 锳九歲從母汲，母墮井，锳呼救未至，亦躍入井，救至，引以出，俱不死。

translations.literal: At nine Ying followed his mother to draw water; his mother fell into the well; Ying cried for help but before rescue arrived he too leapt into the well; when rescue came they were pulled out, and both survived.
translations.idiomatic: At nine Ying followed his mother to draw water. His mother fell into the well. Ying cried for help, but before rescue arrived he too leapt into the well. When rescue came they were pulled out, and both survived.

sentences.zh: 中歲遊陝西，一夕忽心痛，曰：「殆吾父病耶？」

translations.literal: In mid-life he traveled in Shaanxi; one evening he suddenly felt heart pain and said: "Could it be that my father is ill?"
translations.idiomatic: In mid-life he traveled in Shaanxi. One evening he suddenly felt heart pain and said: "Could it be that my father is ill?"

sentences.zh: 馳還，父正病，旋卒，哀慟盡禮。

translations.literal: He raced back; his father was indeed ill and soon died; he mourned with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: He raced back. His father was indeed ill and soon died. He mourned with full rites.

sentences.zh: 方冬母病，求醫，途遇盜，衣盡褫，冒寒行數十里，與醫俱歸。

translations.literal: In deep winter his mother fell ill; he sought a doctor; on the road he met bandits who stripped him of all his clothes; he walked dozens of li through the cold and returned with the doctor.
translations.idiomatic: In deep winter his mother fell ill and he sought a doctor. On the road he met bandits who stripped him of all his clothes. He walked dozens of li through the cold and returned with the doctor.

sentences.zh: 李三，江蘇宜興人。

translations.literal: Li San was a native of Yixing in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Li San was from Yixing in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 一目眇，一足跛。

translations.literal: One eye was blind and one foot lame.
translations.idiomatic: One eye was blind and one foot was lame.

sentences.zh: 父死，二兄皆娶，析產，有田六畝、屋四椽、舟一，二兄分田、屋，而畀三以舟。

translations.literal: When his father died, his two elder brothers all married and the property was divided: there were six mu of fields, four rafters of house, and one boat; the two brothers took fields and house and gave San the boat.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, his two elder brothers all married and the property was divided. There were six mu of fields, four rafters of house, and one boat. The two brothers took the fields and house and gave San the boat.

sentences.zh: 迭養母，三奉母食必有肉，母至二兄所，三輒私致甘旨。

translations.literal: They took turns supporting their mother; when San supported her his meals for her always had meat; when the mother went to the two brothers' places, San would secretly send delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: They took turns supporting their mother. When San supported her, his meals for her always had meat. When the mother went to the two brothers' places, San would secretly send delicacies.

sentences.zh: 二兄死，嫂一前死、一嫁，三獨奉母。

translations.literal: The two brothers died; one sister-in-law had died earlier and one remarried; San alone supported their mother.
translations.idiomatic: The two brothers died. One sister-in-law had died earlier and one remarried. San alone supported their mother.

sentences.zh: 晨爨畢，乃以舟應客，或當出五十里外，度盡日不能返，雖重僱不之許。

translations.literal: After finishing the morning cooking he would take the boat to serve travelers; sometimes a job required going fifty li beyond, and he reckoned he could not return in a full day—though offered high pay he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: After finishing the morning cooking he would take the boat to serve travelers. Sometimes a job required going fifty li beyond, and he reckoned he could not return in a full day. Though offered high pay, he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 事母三十年，鄰里稱其孝，撫兄子慈，而教之嚴。

translations.literal: He served his mother for thirty years; neighbors praised his filial piety; he was kind in raising his brothers' sons yet strict in teaching them.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother for thirty years. Neighbors praised his filial piety. He was kind in raising his brothers' sons yet strict in teaching them.

sentences.zh: 母將死，呼孫執手泣曰：「兒學好，毋累汝叔怒！」

translations.literal: When his mother was about to die she called the grandson, took his hand, wept and said: "Child, study well—do not make your uncle angry!"
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was about to die she called the grandson, took his hand, wept, and said: "Child, study well—do not make your uncle angry!"

sentences.zh: 自是不復怒其兄子。

translations.literal: From then on he no longer grew angry at his brothers' sons.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he no longer grew angry at his brothers' sons.

sentences.zh: 張夢維，直隸元城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Mengwei was a native of Yuancheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mengwei was from Yuancheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 縣諸生。

translations.literal: A county licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county licentiate.

sentences.zh: 父晚病風痺，夢維日侍左右，臥起飲食溲溺皆躬自扶持。

translations.literal: His father in later years fell ill with wind paralysis; Mengwei attended him daily at his side, personally supporting him in lying down and rising, eating and drinking, urination and defecation.
translations.idiomatic: His father in later years fell ill with wind paralysis. Mengwei attended him daily at his side, personally supporting him in lying down and rising, eating and drinking, urination and defecation.

sentences.zh: 父愍其勞，呵之去，少退，复前，數年不少懈。

translations.literal: His father pitied his labor and scolded him to leave; he withdrew a little then came forward again; for several years he did not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: His father pitied his labor and scolded him to leave. He withdrew a little, then came forward again. For several years he did not slacken.

sentences.zh: 事母如事父。

translations.literal: He served his mother as he served his father.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother as he served his father.

sentences.zh: 居喪哀毀，準家禮，屏俗習。

translations.literal: In mourning he grieved and wasted away, following household rites and setting aside vulgar customs.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he grieved and wasted away, following household rites and setting aside vulgar customs.

sentences.zh: 弟病疽，為剪髮灼艾，日數省視，及卒，慟甚，幾喪明。

translations.literal: His younger brother fell ill with carbuncle; he cut the brother's hair and cauterized with moxa, visited several times a day; when the brother died he grieved greatly and nearly lost his sight.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother fell ill with carbuncle. He cut the brother's hair and cauterized with moxa, visiting several times a day. When the brother died he grieved greatly and nearly lost his sight.

sentences.zh: 弟妻或詬誶，待之有加，撫孤女逾己出，弟妻卒悟且悔。

translations.literal: His brother's wife sometimes cursed and reviled him; he treated her all the more generously, cherished the orphaned girl beyond his own child, and the brother's wife finally came to understand and repent.
translations.idiomatic: His brother's wife sometimes cursed and reviled him. He treated her all the more generously and cherished the orphaned girl beyond his own child. The brother's wife finally came to understand and repent.

sentences.zh: 少師郡人衛鶴鳴，治程、硃之學。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Wei Heming of his prefecture, who taught Cheng-Zhu learning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Wei Heming of his prefecture, who taught Cheng-Zhu learning.

sentences.zh: 鶴鳴卒，心喪三年。

translations.literal: When Heming died, he observed heart-mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When Heming died, he observed heart-mourning for three years.

sentences.zh: 授弟子孝經、小學，以力行為本。

translations.literal: He instructed disciples in the Classic of Filial Piety and the Elementary Learning, taking earnest practice as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed disciples in the Classic of Filial Piety and the Elementary Learning, taking earnest practice as the foundation.

sentences.zh: 樂太希，湖北通山縣人。

translations.literal: Yue Taixi was a native of Tongshan County in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Taixi was from Tongshan County in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 幼慧，三歲母負以嬉，墮地傷額。

translations.literal: Clever from childhood; at three his mother carried him to play and he fell to the ground, injuring his forehead.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood. At three his mother carried him to play and he fell to the ground, injuring his forehead.

sentences.zh: 祖母問，詭對，恐祖母見憐而怒母也。

translations.literal: When his grandmother asked, he answered falsely, fearing that if his grandmother saw it she would pity him and grow angry at his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When his grandmother asked, he answered falsely, fearing that if his grandmother saw it she would pity him and grow angry at his mother.

sentences.zh: 父疾，抑搔澣濯，晝夜不去側。

translations.literal: When his father fell ill he pressed, scratched, washed, and bathed him, day and night not leaving his side.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill he pressed, scratched, washed, and bathed him, day and night not leaving his side.

sentences.zh: 居喪盡哀，既葬，恆繞墓悲痛。

translations.literal: In mourning he exhausted grief; after the burial he constantly circled the tomb in grief.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he exhausted grief. After the burial he constantly circled the tomb in grief.

sentences.zh: 母疾及喪亦如之，廬墓側居五年。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill and in mourning he did the same, dwelling in a hut beside the tomb for five years.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill and in mourning he did the same, dwelling in a hut beside the tomb for five years.

sentences.zh: 早為諸生，以事親不應試，或延使授經，輒辭，慮違親也。

translations.literal: Early he became a licentiate, but because of caring for parents he did not sit for examinations; when some invited him to teach the classics he always declined, fearing to neglect his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Early he became a licentiate, but because of caring for his parents he did not sit for examinations. When some invited him to teach the classics he always declined, fearing to neglect his parents.

sentences.zh: 親既終，益篤學。

translations.literal: After his parents had both died he pursued learning all the more diligently.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents had both died he pursued learning all the more diligently.

sentences.zh: 董盛祖，雲南黑鹽井人。

translations.literal: Dong Shengzu was a native of Heiyan Well in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shengzu was from Heiyan Well in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 盛祖不知書，早失父，事母謹，起居飲食侍視不少懈。

translations.literal: Shengzu did not know books; he lost his father early and served his mother carefully, attending to her comings and goings, meals and drink, with not the least slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzu did not know books. He lost his father early and served his mother carefully, attending to her comings and goings, meals and drink, with not the least slackening.

sentences.zh: 一妹嫁里中，盛祖出負販，呼妹還侍母，妹亦善事母如盛祖。

translations.literal: One younger sister married within the village; when Shengzu went out to peddle he called the sister back to attend their mother; the sister also served their mother as well as Shengzu.
translations.idiomatic: One younger sister married within the village. When Shengzu went out to peddle he called the sister back to attend their mother. The sister also served their mother as well as Shengzu.

sentences.zh: 盛祖行遇蛇當道，驚曰：「母得無病乎？」

translations.literal: Once on the road Shengzu met a snake blocking the way and startled said: "Could my mother have fallen ill?"
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road Shengzu met a snake blocking the way and said in alarm: "Could my mother have fallen ill?"

sentences.zh: 歸則母方病，呼祖，人皆怪之。

translations.literal: When he returned his mother had just fallen ill and called for Shengzu; everyone marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned his mother had just fallen ill and called for Shengzu. Everyone marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 母喪，哭甚哀，或慟絕，鄰里驚救之，乃甦。

translations.literal: When his mother died he wept very bitterly, sometimes fainting in grief; neighbors startled rescued him and he revived.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he wept very bitterly, sometimes fainting in grief. Neighbors startled rescued him and he revived.

sentences.zh: 盛祖有妻早亡，不更娶。

translations.literal: Shengzu had a wife who died early and he did not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Shengzu had a wife who died early and he did not remarry.

sentences.zh: 或勸之，曰：「娶婦以事親，顧賢者實難。

translations.literal: When some urged him he said: "One takes a wife to serve parents, yet finding a worthy one is truly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged him he said: "One takes a wife to serve one's parents, yet finding a worthy one is truly difficult.

sentences.zh: 脫不賢，將戾吾母，吾能安乎？」

translations.literal: If by chance she is not worthy, she would wrong my mother—how could I be at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: If by chance she is not worthy, she would wrong my mother. How could I be at ease?"

sentences.zh: 卒不娶。

translations.literal: In the end he did not marry.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not marry.

sentences.zh: 未終喪，遂卒。

translations.literal: Before the mourning period ended he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning period ended he died.

sentences.zh: 徐守仁，安徽青陽人。

translations.literal: Xu Shouren was a native of Qingyang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shouren was from Qingyang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 世為農，未嘗讀書。

translations.literal: The family for generations were farmers and had never studied books.
translations.idiomatic: The family for generations were farmers and had never studied books.

sentences.zh: 四歲而孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Orphaned at four, he served his mother filially.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at four, he served his mother filially.

sentences.zh: 得傭直，市酒肉奉母，母呼共食，輒以持齋謝，實不忍分甘也。

translations.literal: When he received hire wages he bought wine and meat to offer his mother; when his mother called him to eat together he always declined on the pretext of keeping vegetarian fast, in truth unwilling to share the delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: When he received hire wages he bought wine and meat to offer his mother. When his mother called him to eat together he always declined on the pretext of keeping vegetarian fast—in truth unwilling to share the delicacies.

sentences.zh: 母歿，哀慟。

translations.literal: When his mother died he grieved and mourned.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he grieved and mourned.

sentences.zh: 既葬，露處墓側，蛇虺不避，里人哀之，為廬舍飲食焉。

translations.literal: After the burial he dwelt exposed beside the tomb, not avoiding snakes and vipers; villagers pitied him and built him a hut for shelter and food.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he dwelt exposed beside the tomb, not avoiding snakes and vipers. Villagers pitied him and built him a hut for shelter and food.

sentences.zh: 守仁並奉其父木主以居，四年，乃還其室，鬚髮皆白。

translations.literal: Shouren also kept his father's spirit tablet to dwell with him; after four years he returned to his room, and his beard and hair had all turned white.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren also kept his father's spirit tablet to dwell with him. After four years he returned to his room, and his beard and hair had all turned white.

sentences.zh: 李鳳翔，直隸武強人。

translations.literal: Li Fengxiang was a native of Wuqiang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengxiang was from Wuqiang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 善事父母。

translations.literal: He was good at serving his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was good at serving his parents.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔以父老，自請佐家事，而督諸弟讀書、習射，應文、武試。

translations.literal: Fengxiang, because his father was old, voluntarily asked to manage household affairs while supervising his younger brothers in reading books and practicing archery, sitting for civil and military examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang, because his father was old, voluntarily asked to manage household affairs while supervising his younger brothers in reading books and practicing archery, and sitting for civil and military examinations.

sentences.zh: 父將終，遺命析產，心憐幼子而未有言。

translations.literal: When his father was about to die he left instructions to divide the property; in his heart he pitied the youngest son but had not spoken of it.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was about to die he left instructions to divide the property. In his heart he pitied the youngest son but had not spoken of it.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔察父意，益以所分三之一。

translations.literal: Fengxiang perceived his father's intent and added one-third of his own share to the youngest's.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang perceived his father's intent and added one-third of his own share to the youngest's.

sentences.zh: 父歾，事母益謹。

translations.literal: When his father died he served his mother all the more carefully.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he served his mother all the more carefully.

sentences.zh: 道光初，滹沱連歲氾溢，閭里盪析，負鳳翔債者二千餘緡，悉焚其券，复散錢濟貧者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang the Hutuo flooded for successive years and the neighborhood was devastated; debtors to Fengxiang owed more than two thousand strings of cash—he burned all their IOUs and again distributed money to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daoguang the Hutuo flooded for successive years and the neighborhood was devastated. Debtors to Fengxiang owed more than two thousand strings of cash. He burned all their IOUs and again distributed money to relieve the poor.

sentences.zh: 又遇旱，所藝蔬果任飢者採食。

translations.literal: Again when drought came, the vegetables and fruits he cultivated he let the hungry pick and eat.
translations.idiomatic: Again when drought came, he let the hungry pick and eat the vegetables and fruits he cultivated.

sentences.zh: 族子早孤，他縣人以迎喪遇盜，皆厚週之。

translations.literal: A clansman's son orphaned early; people from another county who came to receive a coffin met bandits—Fengxiang generously assisted both.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman's son was orphaned early. People from another county who came to receive a coffin met bandits. Fengxiang generously assisted both.

sentences.zh: 或將屠馬，鳳翔贖以歸，馬馴異常畜，鄉人感之，遂無屠馬者。

translations.literal: When some were about to slaughter a horse, Fengxiang redeemed it and brought it home; the horse was tame beyond ordinary livestock; villagers were moved and thereafter no one slaughtered horses.
translations.idiomatic: When some were about to slaughter a horse, Fengxiang redeemed it and brought it home. The horse was tame beyond ordinary livestock. Villagers were moved, and thereafter no one slaughtered horses.

sentences.zh: 卯觀成，雲南恩安人。

translations.literal: Mao Guancheng was a native of En'an in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Guancheng was from En'an in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 父漢而母夷。

translations.literal: His father was Han and his mother Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Han and his mother Yi.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙亂，父死，母被掠，鬻為婢。

translations.literal: During the Wumeng revolt his father died and his mother was seized and sold as a bondmaid.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wumeng revolt his father died and his mother was seized and sold as a bondmaid.

sentences.zh: 亂定，觀成無所依，為昭通禁卒。

translations.literal: When the turmoil settled Guancheng had nowhere to rely on and became a prison guard at Zhaotong.
translations.idiomatic: When the turmoil settled Guancheng had nowhere to rely on and became a prison guard at Zhaotong.

sentences.zh: 父母嘗為聘婦，舅促觀成娶，娶而不與婚。

translations.literal: His parents had once arranged a betrothal for him; his uncle urged Guancheng to marry—he married but did not consummate the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His parents had once arranged a betrothal for him. His uncle urged Guancheng to marry. He married but did not consummate the marriage.

sentences.zh: 三年，舅詰之，曰：「吾非不欲婚也，行將嫁吾未婚之妻，取所直歸吾母。

translations.literal: After three years his uncle questioned him; he said: "It is not that I do not wish to marry; I am about to marry off my unmarried wife and take the price paid to redeem my mother.
translations.idiomatic: After three years his uncle questioned him. He said: "It is not that I do not wish to marry. I am about to marry off my unmarried wife and take the bride-price to redeem my mother.

sentences.zh: 與之婚，情不能割，義亦不可出也。」

translations.literal: If I consummate the marriage, emotionally I could not bear to part from her, and in duty I also could not let her go."
translations.idiomatic: If I consummate the marriage, emotionally I could not bear to part from her, and in duty I also could not let her go."

sentences.zh: 語且泣。

translations.literal: He spoke as he wept.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke as he wept.

sentences.zh: 有義之者，募得六十金，以半贖其母，半為營廬舍，成婚，仍為禁卒以養母。

translations.literal: A man of righteousness took pity and collected sixty taels of gold; half redeemed his mother and half built a hut for him; the marriage was completed, and he remained a prison guard to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: A man of righteousness took pity and collected sixty taels of gold. Half redeemed his mother and half built a hut for him. The marriage was completed, and he remained a prison guard to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 葛大賓，字興森，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Ge Dabin, style Xingsen, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Dabin, style Xingsen, was from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 四歲喪父，哀慟如成人。

translations.literal: He lost his father at four and grieved and mourned like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at four and grieved and mourned like an adult.

sentences.zh: 喪終，值忌日，出主祭，主僕，粉落「葛」字脫，露「週」姓，蓋木工飾周氏廢主為之。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, on a taboo day he brought out the spirit tablet to sacrifice; the tablet had decayed, the powder fell away, the character "Ge" peeled off, exposing the surname "Zhou"—a carpenter had refurbished a discarded Zhou family tablet for it.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended, on a taboo day he brought out the spirit tablet to sacrifice. The tablet had decayed; the powder fell away, the character "Ge" peeled off, exposing the surname "Zhou"—a carpenter had refurbished a discarded Zhou family tablet for it.

sentences.zh: 大賓痛哭引咎，告墓易主。

translations.literal: Dabin wept bitterly and took blame upon himself, informing the tomb and replacing the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Dabin wept bitterly and took blame upon himself, informing the tomb and replacing the tablet.

sentences.zh: 事母鉅細必躬，疾嘗藥，生徒有餽則獻。

translations.literal: In serving his mother great and small matters he must do personally; when she fell ill he tasted the medicine; when disciples brought gifts he presented them to her.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his mother, great and small matters he must do personally. When she fell ill he tasted the medicine. When disciples brought gifts he presented them to her.

sentences.zh: 嘗出客授，獨坐心動，亟還呼母，母出，屋後山遽頹，壓母坐處。

translations.literal: Once when out teaching guests he sat alone and his heart stirred; he hurried back and called his mother; when his mother came out the mountain behind the house suddenly collapsed, crushing where his mother had been sitting.
translations.idiomatic: Once when out teaching guests he sat alone and his heart stirred. He hurried back and called his mother. When his mother came out the mountain behind the house suddenly collapsed, crushing where his mother had been sitting.

sentences.zh: 母歿，飲不入口者五日。

translations.literal: When his mother died he did not let drink pass his lips for five days.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he did not let drink pass his lips for five days.

sentences.zh: 既葬，不脫衰，腰以下縷皆盡。

translations.literal: After the burial he did not remove mourning garments; the hemp strands below the waist all wore through.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he did not remove mourning garments. The hemp strands below the waist all wore through.

sentences.zh: 喪終，祭必哀，兄弟既分居，財盡，大賓復與同居，通財無所私。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he always mourned at sacrifices; after his brothers had already divided households and their wealth was exhausted, Dabin again lived together with them, sharing wealth without private reserve.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he always mourned at sacrifices. After his brothers had already divided households and their wealth was exhausted, Dabin again lived together with them, sharing wealth without private reserve.

sentences.zh: 歿則庀其喪，無子，為立後。

translations.literal: When they died he arranged their funerals; having no sons he established heirs for them.
translations.idiomatic: When they died he arranged their funerals. Having no sons, he established heirs for them.

sentences.zh: 呂斅孚，湖南永定人。

translations.literal: Lü Xuefu was a native of Yongding in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Xuefu was from Yongding in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 父孟卿，貧，以客授自給。

translations.literal: His father Mengqing was poor and supported himself by teaching guests.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mengqing was poor and supported himself by teaching guests.

sentences.zh: 母病將殆，思肉食，斅孚方七歲，貸諸屠，屠不可，泣而歸。

translations.literal: When his mother fell critically ill she longed for meat; Xuefu was just seven; he borrowed from the butcher—the butcher refused; he wept and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell critically ill she longed for meat. Xuefu was just seven. He borrowed from the butcher—the butcher refused. He wept and returned.

sentences.zh: 聞母呻吟，益痛，內念股肉可啗母，取廚刀礪使利，割右股四寸許，授其女弟，方五歲，令就爐火炙以進。

translations.literal: Hearing his mother's moans he grew more pained; inwardly thinking that flesh from his thigh could feed his mother, he took a kitchen knife, whetted it sharp, cut four cun or so from his right thigh, gave it to his young sister—just five—and had her roast it over the hearth fire and present it.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his mother's moans he grew more pained. Inwardly thinking that flesh from his thigh could feed his mother, he took a kitchen knife, whetted it sharp, cut four cun or so from his right thigh, gave it to his young sister—just five—and had her roast it over the hearth fire and present it.

sentences.zh: 母疾良已，孟卿歸，察斅孚足微跛，得其狀，與母持以哭。

translations.literal: His mother's illness recovered fully; when Mengqing returned he noticed Xuefu's foot was slightly lame, learned what had happened, and he and the mother held him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's illness recovered fully. When Mengqing returned he noticed Xuefu's foot was slightly lame, learned what had happened, and he and the mother held him and wept.

sentences.zh: 斅孚曰：「毋然，兒固無所苦也。」

translations.literal: Xuefu said: "Do not be so; I am truly without suffering."
translations.idiomatic: Xuefu said: "Do not be so. I am truly without suffering."

sentences.zh: 鄉人皆嗟異稱孝童。

translations.literal: Villagers all sighed in wonder and called him the Filial Child.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers all sighed in wonder and called him the Filial Child.

sentences.zh: 長為諸生，學政溫忠翰疏聞，尋除華容訓導。

translations.literal: Grown up he became a licentiate; Educational Commissioner Wen Zhonghan memorialized reporting it; soon he was appointed director of studies at Huarong.
translations.idiomatic: Grown up he became a licentiate. Educational Commissioner Wen Zhonghan memorialized reporting it. Soon he was appointed director of studies at Huarong.

sentences.zh: 孟卿亦嘗刲股愈父病，然斅孚割股時，初不知父有是事也。

translations.literal: Mengqing had also once cut flesh from his thigh to cure his father's illness, yet when Xuefu cut his flesh he did not at first know his father had done such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: Mengqing had also once cut flesh from his thigh to cure his father's illness, yet when Xuefu cut his flesh he did not at first know his father had done such a thing.

sentences.zh: 王子明，甘肅通渭人。

translations.literal: Wang Ziming was a native of Tongwei in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziming was from Tongwei in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 事母孝。

translations.literal: He served his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 出為客，蔬果新出，必遙獻乃食。

translations.literal: When away as a guest, whenever fruits or vegetables were newly available, he had to offer them from afar before he would eat.
translations.idiomatic: When traveling away from home, whenever fresh fruits or vegetables appeared, he would send them home as an offering to his mother before he ate.

sentences.zh: 嘗赴試，母聞桃香久不散，女曰：「此必吾兄所獻。」

translations.literal: Once when he went to sit for an examination, his mother smelled the scent of peaches lingering long; his sister said: "This must be what my elder brother offered."
translations.idiomatic: Once when he went to sit for an examination, his mother smelled peach fragrance that lingered for a long time. His sister said, "This must be what my elder brother sent."

sentences.zh: 記其日，歸驗之，果然。

translations.literal: She noted the day; when he returned they verified it—it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: She noted the day. When he returned they checked, and it was indeed so.

sentences.zh: 馮星明，甘肅秦安人。

translations.literal: Feng Xingming was a native of Qin'an in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingming was from Qin'an in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 為營卒，戍龍山。

translations.literal: He served as a barracks soldier, garrisoned at Longshan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a barracks soldier, garrisoned at Longshan.

sentences.zh: 食新韭，置諸案，叩首。

translations.literal: When he ate fresh chives, he placed them on the table and kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: When he ate fresh chives, he placed them on the table and kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 同伍問之，曰：「以獻母。」

translations.literal: His comrades asked him; he said: "To offer to my mother."
translations.idiomatic: His comrades asked him. He said, "To offer to my mother."

sentences.zh: 咸以為迂。

translations.literal: They all thought him impractical.
translations.idiomatic: They all thought him impractical.

sentences.zh: 或歸候其母，母曰：「他日吾假寐，夢兒以韭食我，覺，猶有餘香。」

translations.literal: Someone returned to visit his mother; the mother said: "The other day I dozed; I dreamed my son fed me chives; when I awoke, the fragrance still lingered."
translations.idiomatic: Someone returned to visit his mother. The mother said, "The other day I dozed off and dreamed my son fed me chives. When I awoke, the fragrance still lingered."

sentences.zh: 叩其日，星明獻韭時也。

translations.literal: They pressed for the day—it was when Xingming had offered chives.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed for the day—it was when Xingming had offered chives.

sentences.zh: 張元翰，直隸南皮人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanhan was a native of Nanpi in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanhan was from Nanpi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年舉人，除獲鹿教諭，遷知縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he passed the provincial examination, was appointed director of studies at Huolu, and was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Guangxu he passed the provincial examination, was appointed director of studies at Huolu, and was promoted to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 方謁京師，父嗣陶時為萬全教諭，卒官。

translations.literal: Just as he was paying respects in the capital, his father Sitao was then director of studies at Wanquan and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was paying respects in the capital, his father Sitao was then director of studies at Wanquan and died in office.

sentences.zh: 元翰奔赴慟哭，幾不能勝。

translations.literal: Yuanhan rushed there and wept in grief, nearly unable to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan rushed there and wept in grief, nearly unable to bear it.

sentences.zh: 居喪三年，悉用古禮。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for three years, entirely using ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: He observed mourning for three years, entirely using ancient rites.

sentences.zh: 喪終，以知縣待缺河南，奉母赴官，攝澠池、寧陵諸縣。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, as magistrate awaiting a vacancy in Henan, he brought his mother to his post and acted as magistrate for Mianchi, Ningling, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, as magistrate awaiting a vacancy in Henan, he brought his mother to his post and acted as magistrate for Mianchi, Ningling, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 方有事於考城，而母遽卒，元翰以父母卒皆不克視終事，大痛。

translations.literal: Just as he was occupied with matters at Kaocheng, his mother suddenly died; Yuanhan, because for neither parent had he been able to attend their final moments, was deeply pained.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was occupied with matters at Kaocheng, his mother suddenly died. Yuanhan, having been unable to attend the final moments of either parent, was deeply pained.

sentences.zh: 將歸葬，自為文祭告，憑棺一慟而絕。

translations.literal: About to return for burial, he himself composed a text to announce and inform at the sacrifice; leaning on the coffin he gave one burst of grief and expired.
translations.idiomatic: About to return for burial, he himself composed a text to announce and inform at the sacrifice. Leaning on the coffin he gave one burst of grief and expired.

sentences.zh: 俞鴻慶，湖南善化人。

translations.literal: Yu Hongqing was a native of Shanhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hongqing was from Shanhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 光緒十八年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Guangxu he passed the metropolitan examination, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 事父母篤孝。

translations.literal: He served his parents with deep filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He served his parents with deep filial piety.

sentences.zh: 官京師，歲必乞假歸省。

translations.literal: While holding office in the capital, every year he would beg leave to return and visit his parents.
translations.idiomatic: While holding office in the capital, every year he would beg leave to return and visit his parents.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，母歾，鴻慶方自西安還京師，聞喪奔還，哀慟若不欲生。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year his mother died; Hongqing had just returned from Xi'an to the capital; hearing of the bereavement he rushed back, grieving as if he did not wish to live.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year his mother died. Hongqing had just returned from Xi'an to the capital. Hearing of the bereavement he rushed back, grieving as if he did not wish to live.

sentences.zh: 父年已八十，衰病，鴻慶跬步不去側，婉容愉色，依慕如少時。

translations.literal: His father was already eighty, frail and ill; Hongqing did not leave his side for a step; gentle countenance and pleased expression, clinging and adoring as in his youth.
translations.idiomatic: His father was already eighty, frail and ill. Hongqing did not leave his side for a step, with gentle countenance and pleased expression, clinging and adoring as in his youth.

sentences.zh: 冬夜必數起省視，或竟夕不眠。

translations.literal: On winter nights he must rise several times to look in on him, sometimes staying awake the whole night.
translations.idiomatic: On winter nights he must rise several times to look in on him, sometimes staying awake the whole night.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，父歾，鴻慶慟甚，以毀卒，距父勿方匝月。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year his father died; Hongqing grieved intensely and died from the destruction of mourning, barely a full month after his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year his father died. Hongqing grieved intensely and died from the destruction of mourning, barely a full month after his father's death.

sentences.zh: 姜瑢，雲南習峨人。

translations.literal: Jiang Rong was a native of Xier in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Rong was from Xier in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 父文柄，嘗遠遊，瑢裹糧行求，得以歸。

translations.literal: His father Wenbing once traveled far; Rong wrapped dry provisions and went seeking, and brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenbing once traveled far. Rong wrapped dry provisions and went seeking, and brought him home.

sentences.zh: 貧，析薪治圃以養。

translations.literal: Poor, he split firewood and tended a garden to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he split firewood and tended a garden to support them.

sentences.zh: 父嗜飲，日必具酒，家益貧，父為罷飲。

translations.literal: His father loved drink; every day he must provide wine; the family grew poorer; the father stopped drinking on their account.
translations.idiomatic: His father loved drink. Every day he must provide wine. The family grew poorer, and the father stopped drinking on their account.

sentences.zh: 命子跪而請，翌日偕樵於山，買酒歸，共勸酣飲，日以為常。

translations.literal: He ordered his son to kneel and plead; the next day they went together to gather firewood on the mountain, bought wine returning, and together urged him to drink deeply—it became their daily custom.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his son to kneel and plead. The next day they went together to gather firewood on the mountain, bought wine on the way home, and together urged him to drink deeply—it became their daily custom.

sentences.zh: 父歾，輒提父嘗飲壺沽酒，哭於墓，人稱其圃為「孝子圃」。

translations.literal: When his father died, he would take his father's drinking pot to buy wine and weep at the tomb; people called his garden the "Garden of the Filial Son."
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he would take his father's drinking pot to buy wine and weep at the tomb. People called his garden the "Garden of the Filial Son."

sentences.zh: 湯淵，江蘇常熟人。

translations.literal: Tang Yuan was a native of Changshu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yuan was from Changshu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 八歲喪父。

translations.literal: He lost his father at eight.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at eight.

sentences.zh: 母茅紡織不稍休，淵見輒淚下。

translations.literal: His mother Mao spun and wove without a moment's rest; when Yuan saw it tears would fall.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Mao spun and wove without a moment's rest. When Yuan saw it, tears would fall.

sentences.zh: 少長，為負販，勸母暫休，母曰：「休，不且餒死耶？」

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older, he became a porter-peddler; he urged his mother to rest briefly; his mother said: "If I rest, will we not starve to death?"
translations.idiomatic: When he grew somewhat older, he became a porter-peddler. He urged his mother to rest briefly. His mother said, "If I rest, will we not starve to death?"

sentences.zh: 淵大慟。

translations.literal: Yuan wailed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wailed greatly.

sentences.zh: 客至，母擎茗椀呼淵持以出，淵跪而受，自責貧不能具僕婢也。

translations.literal: When guests came, his mother would lift the tea bowl and call Yuan to carry it out; Yuan knelt to receive it, blaming himself that poverty kept him from providing servants.
translations.idiomatic: When guests came, his mother would lift the tea bowl and call Yuan to carry it out. Yuan knelt to receive it, blaming himself that poverty kept him from providing servants.

sentences.zh: 娶，生子而婦亡，或勸再娶，曰：「吾已有子，何忍分養母力以養婦？」

translations.literal: He married; a son was born and his wife died; some urged him to remarry; he said: "I already have a son—how could I bear to divert strength for supporting my mother to support a wife?"
translations.idiomatic: He married. A son was born and his wife died. Some urged him to remarry. He said, "I already have a son—how could I bear to divert strength for supporting my mother to support a wife?"

sentences.zh: 竟以鰥終。

translations.literal: He ended as a widower for life.
translations.idiomatic: He remained a widower for life.

sentences.zh: 母卒，哀號動行路。

translations.literal: When his mother died, his wailing moved those on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his wailing moved those on the road.

sentences.zh: 其後家稍裕，方冬，有被而無褥，曰：「吾母昔無此也。」

translations.literal: Later the family grew somewhat comfortable; in deep winter he had a quilt but no mattress; he said: "My mother once had not even this."
translations.idiomatic: Later the family grew somewhat comfortable. In deep winter he had a quilt but no mattress. He said, "My mother once had not even this."

sentences.zh: 將卒，命市棺視殯母之費。

translations.literal: About to die, he ordered a coffin bought matching the cost of his mother's burial.
translations.idiomatic: About to die, he ordered a coffin bought matching the cost of his mother's burial.

sentences.zh: 魏興，直隸新城人。

translations.literal: Wei Xing was a native of Xincheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xing was from Xincheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 早喪父，興與弟繼宗皆入伍。

translations.literal: His father died early; Xing and his younger brother Jizong both entered military service.
translations.idiomatic: His father died early. Xing and his younger brother Jizong both entered military service.

sentences.zh: 繼宗戰死，興以母老，出伍為樵以養。

translations.literal: Jizong died in battle; Xing, because his mother was old, left service to gather firewood and support her.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong died in battle. Xing, because his mother was old, left service to gather firewood and support her.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，米貴，興以米奉母，而自食糟糠，恆不飽。

translations.literal: In a famine year rice was dear; Xing gave rice to his mother while he himself ate chaff and husks, always without his fill.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year rice was dear. Xing gave rice to his mother while he himself ate chaff and husks, always without his fill.

sentences.zh: 興亦老，樵不足，毀屋，伐屋後樹以鬻。

translations.literal: Xing also grew old; firewood was not enough; he demolished the house and felled the trees behind the house to sell.
translations.idiomatic: Xing also grew old. Firewood was not enough. He demolished the house and felled the trees behind the house to sell.

sentences.zh: 安康諸生張鵬翼聞其事，過興，見興侍母左右扶持如童子，因問其鄰魏叟：「與其母日何食？」

translations.literal: Ankang licentiate Zhang Pengyi heard of the matter; passing by Xing he saw Xing attending his mother left and right, supporting her like a child; he therefore asked his neighbor old man Wei: "What do he and his mother eat each day?"
translations.idiomatic: Ankang licentiate Zhang Pengyi heard of the matter. Passing by Xing he saw Xing attending his mother on either side, supporting her like a child. He therefore asked his neighbor old man Wei, "What do he and his mother eat each day?"

sentences.zh: 鄰曰：「興敢包穀，母食麥。」

translations.literal: The neighbor said: "Xing dares eat sorghum; his mother eats wheat."
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor said, "Xing dares eat sorghum; his mother eats wheat."

sentences.zh: 鵬翼大嗟異，以其事白知府，月予以粟，興母子始得飽。

translations.literal: Pengyi sighed greatly in wonder, reported the matter to the prefect, who monthly granted them grain; mother and son at last ate their fill.
translations.idiomatic: Pengyi sighed greatly in wonder and reported the matter to the prefect, who monthly granted them grain. Mother and son at last ate their fill.

sentences.zh: 戴兆笨，安徽旌德人。

translations.literal: Dai Zhaoben was a native of Jingde in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhaoben was from Jingde in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 少從父業縫紉，十三喪母，盡禮，事後母如母。

translations.literal: Young he followed his father's trade in sewing; at thirteen his mother died—he performed the full rites and served his stepmother as his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Young he followed his father's trade in sewing. At thirteen his mother died—he performed the full rites and served his stepmother as his mother.

sentences.zh: 父病噎，亦減飲食，百方療父，不得，則刲肱糜以進，終不愈。

translations.literal: His father fell ill with choking dysphagia; he also reduced his food and drink; in a hundred ways he treated his father without success, then cut flesh from his arm, made gruel, and presented it—his father still did not recover.
translations.idiomatic: His father fell ill with choking dysphagia. He also reduced his food and drink. In a hundred ways he treated his father without success, then cut flesh from his arm, made gruel, and presented it—his father still did not recover.

sentences.zh: 慟甚，廬墓側，朝夕稽顙。

translations.literal: Grieving deeply, he built a hut by the tomb and morning and evening kowtowed.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving deeply, he built a hut by the tomb and morning and evening kowtowed.

sentences.zh: 時歸省後母，呼妻出，戒以善侍養，不入其室。

translations.literal: From time to time he returned to visit his stepmother, called his wife out, admonished her to serve and nourish well, and did not enter their bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time he returned to visit his stepmother, called his wife out, admonished her to serve and nourish well, and did not enter their bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 潘周岱，安徽涇縣人。

translations.literal: Pan Zhoudai was a native of Jing County in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zhoudai was from Jing County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 為竹工，與父同傭，必躬其勞而遺父易且逸者。

translations.literal: A bamboo craftsman; hired out with his father—he must take the labor himself and leave his father the easy and light tasks.
translations.idiomatic: A bamboo craftsman, he was hired out with his father—he must take the labor himself and leave his father the easy and light tasks.

sentences.zh: 父創足，負以往返。

translations.literal: His father injured his foot; he carried him back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: His father injured his foot; he carried him back and forth.

sentences.zh: 老廢，周岱獨應傭，得酒肉時蔬懷歸，燂以進。

translations.literal: When old and disabled, Zhoudai alone answered hire; when he got wine, meat, or seasonal vegetables he carried them home in his bosom, scalded them, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: When old and disabled, Zhoudai alone answered hire. When he got wine, meat, or seasonal vegetables he carried them home in his bosom, scalded them, and presented them.

sentences.zh: 家食，必父母食乃食。

translations.literal: At family meals he must let his parents eat before he ate.
translations.idiomatic: At family meals he would not eat until his parents had eaten.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，奉父母必豐，次以食弟，躬與妻子飽糠覈。

translations.literal: In famine years he served his parents lavishly, next fed his younger brother, while he and his wife and children ate their fill of chaff and husks.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he served his parents lavishly, next fed his younger brother, while he and his wife and children ate their fill of chaff and husks.

sentences.zh: 父母疾，左右侍養無須臾去側。

translations.literal: When his parents fell ill he attended and nourished at their sides without leaving for an instant.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents fell ill he attended and nourished at their sides without leaving for an instant.

sentences.zh: 母家山下泉洌，母病篤，夜半思得泉以飲，周岱挈瓶往，行四十餘裡，鄉晨以泉至。

translations.literal: His mother's natal home had a spring below the mountain, the water clear; when his mother was critically ill, at midnight she longed for that spring to drink; Zhoudai took a jar and went, walked forty-odd li, and at daybreak brought the spring water.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's natal home had a spring below the mountain, the water clear. When his mother was critically ill, at midnight she longed for that spring to drink. Zhoudai took a jar and went, walked forty-odd li, and at daybreak brought the spring water.

sentences.zh: 居喪，旦暮悲號，先後廬墓三年。

translations.literal: In mourning, morning and evening he wailed in grief; in succession he kept tomb huts for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning, morning and evening he wailed in grief. In succession he kept tomb huts for three years.

sentences.zh: 喪既終，夕必詣墓爇香燃燈，如是終其身。

translations.literal: When mourning had ended, every evening he must go to the tomb to burn incense and light lamps—thus to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning had ended, every evening he must go to the tomb to burn incense and light lamps—thus to the end of his life.

sentences.zh: 妻吳亦孝，無違命。

translations.literal: His wife Wu was also filial and never disobeyed a command.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Wu was also filial and never disobeyed a command.

sentences.zh: 張淮，浙江秀水人。

translations.literal: Zhang Huai was a native of Xiushui in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huai was from Xiushui in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 貧，粗識字，為人收田租。

translations.literal: Poor, he knew characters roughly and collected field rents for others.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he knew characters roughly and collected field rents for others.

sentences.zh: 父有心疾，思食羊，非特殺則不食，淮買羊殺以食父。

translations.literal: His father had heart illness and craved mutton—unless specially slaughtered he would not eat; Huai bought sheep, slaughtered them, and fed his father.
translations.idiomatic: His father had heart illness and craved mutton—unless specially slaughtered he would not eat. Huai bought sheep, slaughtered them, and fed his father.

sentences.zh: 思出遊，則賃肩輿侍以出，窮日乃還。

translations.literal: When his father wished to go out touring, he hired a shoulder-sedan chair and attended him out, returning only at day's end.
translations.idiomatic: When his father wished to go out touring, he hired a shoulder-sedan chair and attended him out, returning only at day's end.

sentences.zh: 父疾數年，凡所思，百方致之，不稍怠。

translations.literal: His father's illness lasted several years; whatever he desired, in a hundred ways he procured it, never slackening slightly.
translations.idiomatic: His father's illness lasted several years. Whatever his father desired, in a hundred ways he procured it, never slackening slightly.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，刲肱進，卒不治。

translations.literal: When the illness grew critical he cut flesh from his arm and presented it—still he could not be cured.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness grew critical he cut flesh from his arm and presented it—still he could not be cured.

sentences.zh: 同時張廷標，為衣工。

translations.literal: At the same time Zhang Tingbiao was a garment maker.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Zhang Tingbiao was a garment maker.

sentences.zh: 奉母，常效市中兒嬉戲以娛母。

translations.literal: Serving his mother, he often imitated street children at play to amuse her.
translations.idiomatic: Serving his mother, he often imitated street children at play to amuse her.

sentences.zh: 一日鄰家火，負母出，遷祀先之具，而不及他器用。

translations.literal: One day a neighbor's house caught fire; he carried his mother out, moved the items for sacrificing ancestors, but did not attend to other utensils.
translations.idiomatic: One day a neighbor's house caught fire. He carried his mother out, moved the items for sacrificing ancestors, but did not attend to other utensils.

sentences.zh: 節所入為弟娶婦，而終身不自娶。

translations.literal: He saved his earnings to marry a wife for his younger brother, and through life never married himself.
translations.idiomatic: He saved his earnings to marry a wife for his younger brother, and through life never married himself.

sentences.zh: 縣人與淮稱「二孝子」，道光初年事也。

translations.literal: County people with Huai were called "the two filial sons"—events of the early Daoguang era.
translations.idiomatic: County people with Huai were called "the two filial sons"—events of the early Daoguang era.

sentences.zh: 胡其愛，江南桐城人。

translations.literal: Hu Qi'ai was a native of Tongcheng in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Qi'ai was from Tongcheng in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 為人傭而養母。

translations.literal: He hired himself out to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He hired himself out to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 母病疲癃，其愛日夕在左右，視臥起飲食。

translations.literal: His mother was ill with paralysis and infirmity; Qi'ai was day and night at her side, watching her lying, rising, eating, and drinking.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was ill with paralysis and infirmity. Qi'ai was day and night at her side, watching her lying, rising, eating, and drinking.

sentences.zh: 出就傭，具晨餐，度午不能歸，出勺米付鄰媼，囑代爨，必拜。

translations.literal: Going out to hire, he prepared the morning meal; estimating he could not return by noon, he took out a spoonful of rice and gave it to a neighboring old woman, entrusting her to cook on his behalf—always bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Going out to hire, he prepared the morning meal. Estimating he could not return by noon, he took out a spoonful of rice and gave it to a neighboring old woman, entrusting her to cook on his behalf—always bowing.

sentences.zh: 鄰媼止之，行數里外，复遙拜。

translations.literal: The neighboring old woman would stop him; several li outside he would again bow from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The neighboring old woman would stop him. Several li outside he would again bow from afar.

sentences.zh: 夜必歸，為母滌中裙廁牏。

translations.literal: He must return at night and washed his mother's under-skirts and privy.
translations.idiomatic: He must return at night and washed his mother's under-skirts and privy.

sentences.zh: 在傭家得肉食，即請歸遺母。

translations.literal: At the employer's when he got meat he would immediately ask leave to return and give it to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At the employer's when he got meat he would immediately ask leave to return and give it to his mother.

sentences.zh: 母出觀優，負以往，夜則負以還。

translations.literal: When his mother went out to watch opera, he carried her there; at night he carried her back.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother went out to watch opera, he carried her there. At night he carried her back.

sentences.zh: 欲往戚黨家，亦如之。

translations.literal: When she wished to visit kinsmen and friends, it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: When she wished to visit kinsmen and friends, it was the same.

sentences.zh: 母歿，負土為墳，居悒悒而卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died he piled earth for a grave, lived in dejection, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he piled earth for a grave, lived in dejection, and died.

sentences.zh: 方其明，亦桐城人。

translations.literal: Fang Qiming was also from Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qiming was also from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 亦為傭而養母，母亦病疲癃。

translations.literal: He also hired himself out to support his mother; his mother was also ill with paralysis and infirmity.
translations.idiomatic: He also hired himself out to support his mother. His mother was also ill with paralysis and infirmity.

sentences.zh: 其明慮出傭母飢渴，乃棄傭為丐，負母以出，得食必先母。

translations.literal: Qiming worried that going out to hire his mother would hunger and thirst; he abandoned hiring and became a beggar, carrying his mother out; whatever food he got he always gave his mother first.
translations.idiomatic: Qiming worried that going out to hire his mother would hunger and thirst. He abandoned hiring and became a beggar, carrying his mother out. Whatever food he got he always gave his mother first.

sentences.zh: 母卒，乃為圃，時荷鋤而泣曰：「昔為乞，苦飢寒，不離母側；

translations.literal: When his mother died he then made a garden; sometimes shouldering his hoe he wept, saying: "Formerly as a beggar I suffered hunger and cold but never left my mother's side;
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he then made a garden. Sometimes shouldering his hoe he wept, saying, "Formerly as a beggar I suffered hunger and cold but never left my mother's side;

sentences.zh: 今稍足衣食，思母不可得矣！」

translations.literal: Now I am slightly provided with clothes and food—thinking of my mother, I cannot have her back!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I am slightly provided with clothes and food—thinking of my mother, I cannot have her back!"

sentences.zh: 鄧成珠，福建泰宁人。

translations.literal: Deng Chengzhu was a native of Taining in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Chengzhu was from Taining in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 亦為傭而養母。

translations.literal: He also hired himself out to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He also hired himself out to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 傭所距家遠，日乞米一合，昧旦送母所，還執傭。

translations.literal: The place of hire was far from home; daily he begged one ge of rice, at dawn dark sent it to his mother's place, and returned to take up his hire.
translations.idiomatic: The place of hire was far from home. Daily he begged one ge of rice, at dawn dark sent it to his mother's place, and returned to take up his hire.

sentences.zh: 母盲不能炊，乃負母依主家傍舍，朝夕為具食。

translations.literal: His mother was blind and could not cook; he then carried his mother to lodge in a side hut by the master's house, morning and evening preparing food for her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was blind and could not cook. He then carried his mother to lodge in a side hut by the master's house, morning and evening preparing food for her.

sentences.zh: 主或以為言，成珠曰：「成珠自減餐奉母，不敢重累主人也。」

translations.literal: The master sometimes spoke of it; Chengzhu said: "Chengzhu himself reduces his meals to support his mother—I dare not heavily burden the master again."
translations.idiomatic: The master sometimes spoke of it. Chengzhu said, "Chengzhu himself reduces his meals to support his mother—I dare not heavily burden the master again."

sentences.zh: 居五年，母卒，葬畢，辭主人，不知所之。

translations.literal: After five years, his mother died; when the burial was complete, he took leave of his master and went off—no one knew where.
translations.idiomatic: After five years his mother died. When the burial was complete, he took leave of his master and departed; no one knew where he went.

sentences.zh: 張三愛，江南歙縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang San'ai was a native of She County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang San'ai was from She County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 為人役。

translations.literal: He was a hired laborer.
translations.idiomatic: He worked as a hired laborer.

sentences.zh: 事母孝，母病，不能具藥物。

translations.literal: He served his mother filially; when his mother fell ill, he could not fully provide medicines.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his mother. When she fell ill, he could not afford proper medicine.

sentences.zh: 或謂之曰：「汝欲愈母病，盍刲肝？」

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "If you wish your mother's illness to heal, why not cut out your liver?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone told him, "If you want your mother's illness to heal, why not cut out your liver?"

sentences.zh: 三愛禱於叢祠，破腹，肝墮出，以右手劙肝，得指許，左手納於腹，束以白麻。

translations.literal: San'ai prayed at a woodland shrine, split open his belly, and his liver fell out; with his right hand he sliced the liver, obtaining about a finger's breadth; with his left hand he put it back into his belly and bound it with white hemp.
translations.idiomatic: San'ai prayed at a woodland shrine, cut open his belly, and his liver fell out. With his right hand he sliced off about a finger's breadth of liver, tucked it back into his abdomen with his left hand, and bound the wound with white hemp.

sentences.zh: 歸以肝和羹飲母，母良愈，三愛創亦合。

translations.literal: He returned and mixed the liver into a broth for his mother to drink; his mother recovered well, and San'ai's wound also closed.
translations.idiomatic: He went home, mixed the liver into a broth, and fed it to his mother. She recovered fully, and San'ai's wound healed as well.

sentences.zh: 三愛所事主，故嘗為知縣，貧，逋賦，三愛輒代承，被笞，不少懟。

translations.literal: The master whom San'ai served had once been a county magistrate; poor, he owed taxes in arrears—San'ai always took on the debt for him, was beaten with the bamboo, and never talked back.
translations.idiomatic: San'ai's employer had once served as a county magistrate. Impoverished and in arrears on his taxes, he relied on San'ai, who always paid the debts on his behalf, took the beatings, and never talked back.

sentences.zh: 主病且死，命三愛去，三愛勿聽，事主之子如事主。

translations.literal: When the master was ill and near death, he ordered San'ai to leave; San'ai would not listen, and served the master's son as he had served the master.
translations.idiomatic: When his employer fell mortally ill, he told San'ai to leave. San'ai refused and continued to serve the man's son exactly as he had served the father.

sentences.zh: 楊夢益，陝西郃陽人。

translations.literal: Yang Mengyi was a native of Heyang in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Mengyi was from Heyang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 賣菜傭也，事母孝，妻賈力紡織以佐養。

translations.literal: He was a vegetable peddler by trade; he served his mother filially, and his wife sold her labor spinning and weaving to help support them.
translations.idiomatic: He sold vegetables for a living and was devoted to his mother. His wife earned extra income by spinning and weaving to help support the household.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，歲饑，夢益與妻食糠籺，盛米於囊，置其中，熟以奉母。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign, when famine struck the year, Mengyi and his wife ate bran cakes; they put rice in a bag and placed it in the middle, cooked it, and presented it to their mother.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong era, when famine struck, Mengyi and his wife ate bran cakes while keeping rice in a bag at the center of their pot. They cooked it and served the rice to their mother.

sentences.zh: 米盡，將鬻子，族人感而周之，乃止。

translations.literal: When the rice was gone, they were about to sell their son; clansmen were moved and helped them, and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the rice ran out, they were about to sell their son. Moved by their plight, relatives pooled resources to help them, and they abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 閻天倫，甘肅隴​​西人。

translations.literal: Yan Tianlun was a native of Longxi in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tianlun was from Longxi in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 貧，父居僧寺，天倫與妻楊，雞鳴起磨面，及明入市，求父所嗜往饋，午若晡皆然，夜則從父寢。

translations.literal: Poor, his father lived in a Buddhist temple; Tianlun and his wife Yang rose at cockcrow to grind flour, and at dawn entered the market, sought what his father loved, and went to feed him—at noon and at dusk it was always so; at night he slept beside his father.
translations.idiomatic: Impoverished, his father lived in a Buddhist temple. Tianlun and his wife Yang rose at cockcrow to grind flour, then at dawn went to market, bought whatever his father craved, and brought it to him—morning, noon, and dusk alike. At night he slept beside his father.

sentences.zh: 父失明，天倫為茹素，年餘，目復明。

translations.literal: When his father went blind, Tianlun ate only vegetables for more than a year, and his father's eyes regained their sight.
translations.idiomatic: When his father went blind, Tianlun ate only vegetables for more than a year, and his father's eyesight returned.

sentences.zh: 天倫先父卒，楊賣漿為養，如天倫在時。

translations.literal: Tianlun died before his father; Yang sold gruel to support him, as when Tianlun had been alive.
translations.idiomatic: Tianlun died before his father. Yang sold gruel to support her father-in-law just as Tianlun had done.

sentences.zh: 翁卒，力營葬，忌日必祭，終其身。

translations.literal: When the old man died, she labored to arrange the burial; on memorial days she always offered sacrifice, for the rest of her life.
translations.idiomatic: When the old man died, she labored to give him a proper burial and observed memorial rites on the appointed days for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 夏士友，湖北江夏人。

translations.literal: Xia Shiyou was a native of Jiangxia in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Shiyou was from Jiangxia in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 事母孝，傭力以養，不足，則減己食食母。
