translations.literal: He served his mother filially, hiring out his labor to support her; when it was not enough, he reduced his own food to feed his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to his mother and hired himself out to support her. When his earnings fell short, he ate less so she could eat more.

sentences.zh: 鄰或邀食，必先為母具食，然後往。

translations.literal: When neighbors invited him to eat, he always first prepared food for his mother, and only then went.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors invited him to dine, he always prepared his mother's meal first and only then went.

sentences.zh: 寒，語母勿早起，自執炊置食床前，又丁寧囑母善自護，乃出，如是以為常。

translations.literal: In cold weather he told his mother not to rise early; he himself did the cooking and set food by her bed, again and again urging her to take good care of herself, and then went out—thus it was his constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: In cold weather he told his mother not to rise early. He cooked himself, set food by her bed, urged her repeatedly to take care of herself, and only then went out to work—his daily routine.

sentences.zh: 年四十未娶，或愍之，助其娶婦。

translations.literal: At forty he had not yet married; some pitied him and helped him take a wife.
translations.idiomatic: He reached forty without marrying. Moved by his plight, neighbors helped him find a wife.

sentences.zh: 居半載，士友自外歸，婦與姑詬於室，流涕責婦，即日出之。

translations.literal: After half a year, Shiyou returned from outside; his wife and mother-in-law were quarreling in the room. Weeping, he reproached his wife and dismissed her that very day.
translations.idiomatic: After six months Shiyou came home from work to find his wife quarreling with his mother. In tears he rebuked his wife and sent her away that same day.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「出婦，如無後何？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "If you dismiss your wife, what of having no descendants?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "If you send your wife away, what will become of your line?"

sentences.zh: 士友曰：「有婦，欲其孝；

translations.literal: Shiyou said: "Having a wife, one wants her to be filial;
translations.idiomatic: Shiyou said, "One takes a wife hoping she will be filial.

sentences.zh: 有子孫，亦欲其孝。

translations.literal: having sons and grandsons, one also wants them to be filial.
translations.idiomatic: One has children and grandchildren hoping they will be filial.

sentences.zh: 苟不孝，安用婦？

translations.literal: If they are not filial, what use is a wife?
translations.idiomatic: If they are not filial, what use is a wife?

sentences.zh: 安用子孫？」

translations.literal: What use are sons and grandsons?"
translations.idiomatic: What use are children and grandchildren?"

sentences.zh: 年餘，士友疾卒，母哭之慟，鄰有張某感士友孝而不得終事母，月供薪米，終其身。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Shiyou died of illness; his mother wept for him in anguish. A neighbor surnamed Zhang, moved that Shiyou's filial piety had not let him finish serving his mother, monthly supplied firewood and rice for her, for the rest of her life.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Shiyou died of illness, and his mother mourned him bitterly. A neighbor named Zhang, moved that Shiyou's devotion had kept him from finishing his service to his mother, supplied her monthly with firewood and rice for the rest of her life.

sentences.zh: 白長久，甘肅平番人。

translations.literal: Bai Changjiu was a native of Pingfan in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Changjiu was from Pingfan in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，貧，負販奉母，具甘旨。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, poor, he carried goods on his back peddling to support his mother, providing delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, he peddled goods on his back to support his mother and always brought her delicacies.

sentences.zh: 母或不怡，以首抵母，引手披其頸，俟解乃止。

translations.literal: When his mother was displeased, he pressed his head against hers and with his hand stroked her neck, waiting until she was soothed before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was displeased, he pressed his forehead to hers and stroked her neck with his hand, waiting until she calmed before he stopped.

sentences.zh: 里社演劇，負母往觀，侍側說劇中事。

translations.literal: When the village shrine put on plays, he carried his mother to watch and stood at her side explaining the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When the village put on opera at the shrine, he carried his mother to watch and stood beside her narrating the plot.

sentences.zh: 母年八十，長久亦六十，未嘗稍懈。

translations.literal: His mother was eighty, and Changjiu was sixty, yet he never slackened slightly.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was eighty and Changjiu sixty, yet he never slackened in his care.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，青海辦事大臣豫師餽以金，不受。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu reign, Yu Shi, commissioner for Qinghai affairs, presented him with gold; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu era, Yu Shi, the Qinghai commissioner, offered him gold, but he refused it.

sentences.zh: 母卒，朝夕詣墓，饋食三年。

translations.literal: When his mother died, morning and evening he went to the grave and offered food for three years.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, he visited her grave morning and evening with offerings for three years.

sentences.zh: 郭味兒，甘肅禮縣人。

translations.literal: Guo Wei'er was a native of Li County in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei'er was from Li County in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 賣漿，出必拜母，歸亦然。

translations.literal: He sold gruel; whenever he went out he bowed to his mother, and when he returned it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: He sold gruel. Every time he left the house he bowed to his mother, and he did the same when he returned.

sentences.zh: 母嚴，稍不當意即恚，味兒為孺子狀悅母。

translations.literal: His mother was strict; if anything was slightly not to her liking she grew angry, and Wei'er would act like a little child to please her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was stern. At the slightest displeasure she grew angry, and Wei'er would play the coaxing child to cheer her.

sentences.zh: 母苦脛痛，或言瘞枯骨，母當愈，黎明輒攜長鑱徘徊丘隴間，寒暑不間。

translations.literal: His mother suffered pain in her shins; someone said that burying dry bones would cure her. At dawn he always carried a long spade wandering among mounds and ridges, without break through cold or heat.
translations.idiomatic: His mother suffered pain in her shins. Someone said burying dry bones would cure her. At dawn each day he took a long spade and wandered the burial mounds, never pausing through winter or summer.

sentences.zh: 母卒，飲不入口，五日毀卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he took no food or drink; on the fifth day he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he refused food and drink and died of grief on the fifth day.

sentences.zh: 聶宏，陝西鄠縣人。

translations.literal: Nie Hong was a native of Hu County in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Hong was from Hu County in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 賣酒，事親孝，得錢易甘脆奉親。

translations.literal: He sold wine, served his parents filially, and with whatever money he earned exchanged for delicacies to present to them.
translations.idiomatic: He sold wine and was devoted to his parents. Whatever he earned he spent on delicacies for them.

sentences.zh: 母卒，臥父榻側，時省視。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he lay beside his father's couch, checking on him from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, he slept beside his father's couch and looked in on him constantly.

sentences.zh: 畜犬，得餅銜飼母，人以為孝感。

translations.literal: He kept a dog; when it got a cake it carried it in its mouth to feed his mother—people took it as a sign of filial response from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a dog that, when it got a cake, carried it in its mouth to feed his mother. People regarded it as Heaven's reward for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 董阿虎，江南山陽人。

translations.literal: Dong Ahu was a native of Shanyang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ahu was from Shanyang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少喪父，為人擔水，得值養母。

translations.literal: He lost his father young, carried water for others, and with his wages supported his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned of his father young, he carried water for hire and used his wages to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 稍有餘，必具甘旨。

translations.literal: Whenever he had a little surplus, he always provided delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he had anything to spare, he spent it on delicacies for her.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，構茅屋奉母。

translations.literal: After more than ten years he built a thatched hut to house his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years he built a thatched hut for his mother.

sentences.zh: 一日，鄰被火，阿虎負母避，還跪戶外，乞神佑。

translations.literal: One day a neighbor's house caught fire; Ahu carried his mother to safety, then returned and knelt outside the door, begging the gods for protection.
translations.idiomatic: One day a neighbor's house caught fire. Ahu carried his mother to safety, then returned and knelt outside his door, begging the gods for protection.

sentences.zh: 俄左右盡爇，獨阿虎茅屋存。

translations.literal: Soon everything on either side was burned to ashes, yet Ahu's thatched hut alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Soon everything on either side was reduced to ashes, yet Ahu's thatched hut alone stood untouched.

sentences.zh: 張乞人，順天永清人，失其名。

translations.literal: Zhang the Beggar was from Yongqing in Shuntian; his personal name is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang the Beggar was from Yongqing in Shuntian; his given name is unknown.

sentences.zh: 父死，行乞以養母。

translations.literal: When his father died, he went begging to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died, he begged for alms to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 穴土為居，天大雪，知縣魏繼齊過其處，聞歌聲出地中，怪而呼問之，曰：「今日母生日，歌以勸餐耳。」

translations.literal: He dug earth for a dwelling; one day heavy snow fell. County Magistrate Wei Jiqi passed that place, heard singing rise from underground, found it strange, and called out to ask; he said: "Today is my mother's birthday—I sing to encourage her to eat."
translations.idiomatic: He dug an earthen dwelling for them. One day, during heavy snow, County Magistrate Wei Jiqi passed by and heard singing from underground. Astonished, he called out to ask. The beggar said, "Today is my mother's birthday. I sing to encourage her to eat."

sentences.zh: 繼齊命車載其母子至縣，繼齊母畀其母粟及布，繼齊與銀十緡。

translations.literal: Jiqi ordered a cart to carry mother and son to the county seat; Jiqi's mother gave his mother grain and cloth, and Jiqi gave him ten strings of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqi had a cart bring mother and son to the county seat. Jiqi's mother gave the beggar's mother grain and cloth, and Jiqi gave him ten strings of silver.

sentences.zh: 乞人叩頭曰：「官母賜我母，不敢不受；

translations.literal: The beggar kowtowed and said: "The official's mother bestows gifts on my mother—I dare not refuse;
translations.idiomatic: The beggar kowtowed and said, "When the magistrate's mother gives gifts to my mother, I dare not refuse.

sentences.zh: 官賜我，我不敢受。」

translations.literal: what the official bestows on me, I dare not accept."
translations.idiomatic: What the magistrate gives me, I dare not accept."

sentences.zh: 繼齊問其故，曰：「民愚，不知此十緡官何所受之？

translations.literal: Jiqi asked the reason; he said: "This commoner is foolish and does not know from what source the official received these ten strings?
translations.idiomatic: Jiqi asked why. He said, "I am only a foolish commoner. I do not know where the magistrate obtained these ten strings.

sentences.zh: 我母年八十，我年六十​​一，為清白百姓足矣。」

translations.literal: My mother is eighty, I am sixty-one—to be an upright commoner is enough."
translations.idiomatic: My mother is eighty and I am sixty-one. To live as an honest commoner is enough for us."

sentences.zh: 繼齊不復強，將為營室，乞人負其母去，不知所終。

translations.literal: Jiqi did not press him further and was about to build a house for him; the beggar carried his mother away and no one knew his end.
translations.idiomatic: Jiqi did not press him further and offered to build him a house. The beggar carried his mother away, and no one knew what became of them.

sentences.zh: 席慕孔，廣東三水人。

translations.literal: Xi Mukong was a native of Sanshui in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Mukong was from Sanshui in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 善養母。

translations.literal: He was skilled at supporting his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to supporting his mother.

sentences.zh: 嘗娶妻生子。

translations.literal: He once took a wife and had a son.
translations.idiomatic: He once married and had a son.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，田數畝盡鬻，妻怨其貧，求去，遂遣之。

translations.literal: When famine struck the year, he sold off his few mu of fields entirely; his wife resented their poverty and asked to leave, so he sent her away.
translations.idiomatic: When famine came, he sold his few mu of fields. His wife, resenting their poverty, asked to leave, and he let her go.

sentences.zh: 夏秋助人耕穫為傭，冬則乞食以養。

translations.literal: In spring and summer he hired out to help with planting and harvest; in winter he begged for food to support her.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and summer he hired out for planting and harvest work; in winter he begged for food to support her.

sentences.zh: 得餅餌歸食母，得餘羹，啜湆，以肉歸。

translations.literal: Whatever cakes he got he brought home for his mother to eat; if there was leftover broth, he drank the dregs and brought the meat home.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever cakes he obtained he brought home for his mother. If there was leftover broth, he drank the dregs himself and brought the meat home to her.

sentences.zh: 張長松，山東棲霞人。

translations.literal: Zhang Changsong was a native of Qixia in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changsong was from Qixia in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 母瞽，長松出為傭，主人與之食，輒不盡，歸遺母。

translations.literal: His mother was blind; Changsong went out as a hired laborer. When the master gave him food, he never finished it, but brought the remainder home to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was blind. Changsong hired himself out, and whenever his employer gave him food he never finished it, bringing the rest home to his mother.

sentences.zh: 無所事則乞諸鄰里，母食已，乃食其餘。

translations.literal: When he had nothing to do he begged from neighbors; after his mother had eaten, he then ate what remained.
translations.idiomatic: When idle he begged from neighbors. Only after his mother had eaten did he eat what was left.

sentences.zh: 冬大雪，長松病不能出，呼母涕泣言曰：「兒不肖，不能養吾母，乃乞食，母賴以活。

translations.literal: In winter heavy snow fell; Changsong was ill and could not go out. Calling to his mother, weeping, he said: "Your son is unworthy and cannot support my mother—thus I beg for food, and Mother relies on that to live.
translations.idiomatic: One winter, during heavy snow, Changsong fell ill and could not go out. Weeping, he called to his mother and said, "Your son is unworthy and cannot support you—I have had to beg for food, and you have lived on that.

sentences.zh: 今疾憊，母老，可若何？」

translations.literal: Now I am worn out by illness; Mother is old—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I am worn out by sickness, and you are old. What is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 遂死。

translations.literal: He then died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 崔長生，江南邳州人。

translations.literal: Cui Changsheng was a native of Pizhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Changsheng was from Pizhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 生而瘖，手又攣。

translations.literal: From birth he was mute, and his hands were also crippled.
translations.idiomatic: He was born mute, and his hands were crippled as well.

sentences.zh: 為傭養父母，出入必面。

translations.literal: He hired out to support his parents; whenever he went out or came in he always faced them.
translations.idiomatic: He hired himself out to support his parents and always turned his face toward them whenever he left or returned.

sentences.zh: 歲大祲，乞食於市，得糟糠，上父母，自食草根木實以活。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine he begged for food in the market; what chaff and bran he got he gave his parents, while he himself ate roots, bark, and fruit to stay alive.
translations.idiomatic: During a great famine he begged in the market. Whatever chaff and bran he obtained he gave his parents, while he lived on roots, bark, and wild fruit.

sentences.zh: 拾字紙，得遺金，待失者踰月不得。

translations.literal: While gathering waste paper he found lost gold; he waited for the owner more than a month without anyone coming.
translations.idiomatic: While gathering waste paper he found lost gold and waited more than a month for the owner, but no one came.

sentences.zh: 乃易母彘飼之，茁壯蕃息，為父母治送死之具。

translations.literal: He then exchanged it for a sow to feed; it grew strong and multiplied, and with it he prepared funeral goods for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He then used it to buy a sow to raise. The pig thrived and multiplied, and with the proceeds he prepared his parents' funeral goods.

sentences.zh: 喪父母，舁葬於中野，遂去，不知所終。

translations.literal: When his parents died, he shouldered them and buried them in the open countryside, then departed—no one knew his end.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents died, he carried them on his shoulders and buried them in open country, then departed. No one knew what became of him.

sentences.zh: 榮孝子，河南遂平人。

translations.literal: Rong the Filial Son was a native of Suiping in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong the Filial Son was from Suiping in Henan.

sentences.zh: 幼痴聾，無名。

translations.literal: From childhood he was dull and deaf, and had no personal name.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was dull and deaf, and had no personal name.

sentences.zh: 家本饒，後中落，貧甚。

translations.literal: His family had once been well-off, but later fell into decline and was extremely poor.
translations.idiomatic: His family had once been prosperous but later fell into ruin and extreme poverty.

sentences.zh: 父卒，無所居，奉母居棲流鋪。

translations.literal: When his father died they had nowhere to live; he housed his mother in a refugee shelter.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died they had nowhere to live. He lodged his mother in a refugee shelter.

sentences.zh: 出乞食，擇所得供母，自食其餘。

translations.literal: Going out to beg, he chose what he obtained to supply his mother and ate the remainder himself.
translations.idiomatic: He went out begging, chose the best of what he received for his mother, and ate the rest himself.

sentences.zh: 得少，則但供母，而自忍飢歸。

translations.literal: If he got little, he supplied only his mother and returned himself enduring hunger.
translations.idiomatic: If he obtained little, he gave it all to his mother and went home hungry himself.

sentences.zh: 見母必叩頭，食必跪進。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw his mother he kowtowed; whenever he served food he knelt to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw his mother he kowtowed. Whenever he served food he knelt to present it.

sentences.zh: 母食則起而舞，食減則泣。

translations.literal: When his mother ate he rose and danced; when she ate less he wept.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother ate he rose and danced for joy. When she ate less he wept.

sentences.zh: 母或故減食以食子，則泣不受。

translations.literal: If his mother deliberately reduced her food to feed her son, he wept and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: If his mother deliberately ate less to feed him, he wept and refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 母七十餘卒，縣人為具斂，朝暮泣，終其身。

translations.literal: When his mother died past seventy, the county people provided the shroud; morning and evening he wept, for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died past seventy, county residents provided her burial garments. He wept morning and evening for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 吏以孝子旌其楣，亦不知孝子為何名也。

translations.literal: The officials honored his door lintel as "Filial Son," yet no one knew what the Filial Son's name was.
translations.idiomatic: Officials honored his door lintel with the title "Filial Son," yet no one knew the Filial Son's given name.

sentences.zh: 卒亦七十餘。

translations.literal: When he died he was also past seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He too died past the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 無錫二孝子，皆失其姓氏。

translations.literal: Two filial sons of Wuxi—both have lost their surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Two filial sons of Wuxi—both surnames are unknown.

sentences.zh: 其一瞽，磨粉為業，事母至孝，竭力供甘旨。

translations.literal: One was blind, grinding flour for a living; he served his mother with utmost filial piety, exerting all his strength to provide delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: One was blind and ground flour for a living. He served his mother with utmost devotion, straining every effort to provide delicacies.

sentences.zh: 年至四十餘復明，人皆異之。

translations.literal: Past forty his eyes regained sight—everyone marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Past forty his eyesight returned, to everyone's astonishment.

sentences.zh: 其一啞，行乞得錢以養母，必具酒脯。

translations.literal: One was mute; begging he got money to support his mother and always provided wine and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: The other was mute. Begging for money to support his mother, he always bought wine and dried meat for her.

sentences.zh: 母卒，食必祭，祭必伏地號痛。

translations.literal: When his mother died, at every meal he offered sacrifice; at every sacrifice he prostrated himself on the ground wailing.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he made offerings before every meal, each time prostrating himself on the ground and wailing.

sentences.zh: 既葬，哭於墓，見者皆感。

translations.literal: After the burial, he wept at the grave; all who saw it were moved.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he wept at the grave, moving all who saw him.

sentences.zh: 啞孝子，無姓氏，或曰雲南昆明人。

translations.literal: The mute filial son, surname unknown—some say he was from Kunming in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The mute filial son, surname unknown—some say he was from Kunming in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 家有母，老矣，行乞以養。

translations.literal: He had a mother at home, already old; he went begging to support her.
translations.idiomatic: He had an aged mother at home and begged for alms to support her.

sentences.zh: 得食必奉母，母食然後食。

translations.literal: When he obtained food he always presented it to his mother; only after his mother had eaten did he eat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he obtained food he always presented it to his mother, and only after she had eaten did he eat.

sentences.zh: 母或怒，嬉戲拜且舞，必母樂乃已。

translations.literal: When his mother was angry, he played and bowed and danced until she was pleased before he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was angry, he played the fool, bowing and dancing until she was pleased before he stopped.

sentences.zh: 得錢密投諸井，母卒，鄉人有欲醵錢以助斂者，與如井，數數指水中，鄉人為出錢，營殮且葬。

translations.literal: When he obtained money he secretly threw it into a well; when his mother died, villagers wished to collect money to assist with the burial; he led them to the well and repeatedly pointed at the water; the villagers took out the money and arranged the encoffining and burial.
translations.idiomatic: When he obtained money he secretly threw it into a well. When his mother died, villagers wished to collect money to assist with the burial. He led them to the well and repeatedly pointed at the water. The villagers retrieved the money and arranged the encoffining and burial.

sentences.zh: 事畢，遠遊不知所終。

translations.literal: When the matter was complete, he traveled far away and no one knew his end.
translations.idiomatic: When all was done, he traveled far away, and no one knew what became of him.
